# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L245-L249


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The value of _duration is used to update the lockDuration of a player.
Before being pushed to the playerSettings, it is checked that it is less than the MaxLockDuration.
The comparison is done in uint256 for _duration and StorageKey.MaxLockDuration which is set in uint32 but upcast to uint256 via configStorage.getUnit().

_duration is then downcast to uint32 which creates the issue with the following scenarios possible as a result.

Scenario 1: Given a user passed the MaxLockDuration check and has no existing locked tokens, the execution of setLockDuration updates their settings and ends. If  the downcasted _duration value is 0 or less than lockdrop.minLockDuration it will be set to minLockDuration which may not be the intention of the user. Limiting their return for locking tokens

Scenario 2: Given a user passed the MaxLockDuration check and has locked tokens, the downcasted _duration value can create a DOS where the block.timestamp + _duration is less than the current unlockTime which was may not be the intention of the user

## Proof of Concept
Scenario 1 Code Snippet: https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L347-L360

Scenario 2 Code Snippet: https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L249-L261

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Accept uint32 for _duration and perform MaxLockDuration comparison in uint32 instead of uint256

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L244-L272


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
A user can reduce a lockup time that was previously set, breaking one of the invariants of the protocol. This could for example be used to harvest bonus undeserved schnibbles. 

## Proof of Concept
Proof of Concept
The function `setLockDuration` resets the lock duration for every token. While doing this, it uses the newly set duration plus `lastLockTime`, which is the last point in time when a token was locked.

The issue arises because `setLockDuration` does not update the token's `lastLockTime`. As a result, after the initial locking, a user can set `setLockDuration` to a bigger value, harvest rewards for a longer lock, and then use `setLockDuration` again with the stale `lastLockTime` to reduce the unlock time and receive undeserved rewards.

Example:
A user locks some tokens at time `t` with a lock duration of 30 days.

After 20 days, the user calls setLockDuration and sets it to 60 days.

At this point, unlockTime is correctly set to `t + 60`, with the lock duration being 60 days.

Now, `block.timestamp` = `t + 20` and `lastLockTime` = `t`. This allows the user to set the lock duration to 40 days since the following check passes:
```solidity
                if (
                    uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <
                    lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime
                ) {
                    revert LockDurationReducedError();
                }
```
The unlockTime is then set with the stale lastLockTime:
```solidity
                uint32 lastLockTime = lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract]
                    .lastLockTime;
                lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime =
                    lastLockTime +
                    uint32(_duration);
```
This sets unlockTime to `t + 40` days, decreasing the lock time that was previously set to `t + 60`.

## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
`setLockDuration` should set `lastLockTime` to `block.timestamp` after setting unlockTime.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L274-L294
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L382-L384
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L256-L261


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users are able to push `unlockTime` of other users' locks further by locking dust amounts of tokens using `lockOnBehalf`.

## Proof of Concept
The function [lockOnBehalf](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L274C1-L294C6) lets users lock tokens on other's behalf. This will increase the `unlockTime` of the token locked:
```solidity
        lockedToken.unlockTime =
            uint32(block.timestamp) +
            uint32(_lockDuration);
```
As there are no minimum amount checks, an attacker could use dust amounts to easily affect `unlockTime`. At this point the only way out for the funds would be setting the lock duration to a very small value, this is because if it is set to zero funds will be locked for another 30 days(minLockDuration), also note `setLockDuration` will not let a user change his/her duration if it is decreasing the `unlockTime`:
```solidity
                if (
                    uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <
                    lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime
                ) {
                    revert LockDurationReducedError();
                }
```

Example:
User locks some tokens for 30 days at time `t`.

At the end of lock or a day before attacker locks on user's behalf.

Now the user will have to wait for an extra 30 days to withdraw these funds.

In order to prevent this a user would have to repeatedly call `setLockDuration` to decrease its lock duration at many intervals. Otherwise attacker can keep locking to push `unlockTime` further.

## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
You could introduce permission functionality for locking on other's behalf and/or add minimum amount checks for `lockOnBehalf` so that the attack would be expensive.





## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L352-L355


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Users cannot set the token `lockDuration < minLockDuration` (30 days) if they directly call the `lock()` function or set the `lockDuration == 0`, this is not in accordance with the protocol provisions which free users to set the lock duration according to their needs

## Proof of Concept

```solidity
        if (_lockDuration == 0) {
            _lockDuration = lockdrop.minLockDuration;
        }
```

It can be seen from the line of code above, if the user does not set the lock duration at the beginning by calling the `setLockDuration()` function or enter `0` as the value of the lock duration, then the `lockDuration = lockdrop.minLockDuration` which has a value of 30 days. 

`lockdrop.minLockDuration` should only be used when there is a `lockdrop` event

Scenario 

1. Bob does not set the duration of the lock or sets the `lockDuration == 0` with the `setLockDuration()` function
2. Then he call `lock()` function
3. Because `lockDuration == 0`, the value is set to `lockDuration = lockdrop.minLockDuration`, which is 30 days

```solidity
        lockedToken.unlockTime =
            uint32(block.timestamp) +
            uint32(_lockDuration);
```

4. Then the value of `lockedToken.unlockTime` is updated
5. That way, the user cannot set the token lock duration less than that value in the `setLockDuration()` function because there is a check 

```solidity
                if (
                    uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <
                    lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime
                ) {
                    revert LockDurationReducedError();
```

In this way, users who accidentally set `lockDuration == 0` or who don't set it from the start will be the subject of a `lockdrop` event which may not take place and the user will not be able to set the lock token duration as desired.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Consider adding check `lockdrop` event ongoing or not, if yes use the code as above, otherwise revert if `lockDuration` not set


## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The locking behavior will be locked once the remaining time of the `lockDrop` is less than `minLockDuration`. Currently, no check prevents this happening even from the first second of the lockdrop. 

The admin can configure lockDrop periods with the `configureLockdrop`. It allows the admin to set both the start and end periods as well as the minimum amount of time, which the users can lock for. 

Currently there are checks, which prevent the admin to set lockdrops in unachievable times. For example, you can not set lockdrop in the past, or one, which starts after the end period. 

However, setting a `minLockDuration`, which is bigger than the whole duration of the lockdrop is still possible. That means that, until a new lockdrop period is set, the users won't be able to lock funds in the protocol


## Proof of Concept
1. Admin sets a lockDrop period for 1 day with `minLockDuration` of 1 day and 1 hour
2. Users can't use `lock` as they can't satisfy both the `minLockDuration` and the lockDrop period



## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add a check, which will revert if the admin adds unachievable `minLockDuration`
```solidity
if(_lockdropData.end - _lockdropData.start >= _lockdropData.minLockDuration) {
revert LockdropInvalidError();
}
```


## Assessed type

DoS

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Any Malicious user can update the `unlockTime` of another user using `LockManager.sol::lockOnBehalf` function with a very small amount of token/native_currency like 1 wei as `_quantity`. Which can Impact in updating of user's unlockTime.This will no longer allows the user to call `LockManager.sol::unlock` at their original unlockTime Because it got updated due to the Malicious user Action. If the Malicious user continuous to update the innocent user's unlockTime with small amounts like 1 wei even just before the current `unlockTime` ends, then the user's originally `lockedquantity` can no longer be unlocked, it will in the contract forever. It will severely effects the integrity of the system.

## Proof of Concept
```
Function :- lockOnBehalf( address _tokenContract,uint256 _quantity,address _onBehalfOf)

User1 calls -> lockOnBehalf ( token/native currency , quantity , User2)
 
lockDuration of User2 = _lockDuration 
lastLockTime of User2 = (block.timestamp) 
unlockTime of User2 =  (block.timestamp + _lockDuration) 

Lets Assume _lockDuration is 100 secs 
on  90th sec 

Malicious User3 calls -> lockOnBehalf ( token/native currency , quantity , User2)
(tokens/native currency quantity from Malicious user can be very small amount like 1 wei)

lockDuration of User2 = _lockDuration
lastLockTime of User2 = (block.timestamp) = 90 secs
unlockTime of User2 = (block.timestamp + _lockDuration) = 90 secs + 100 secs = 190 secs

Malicious User3 Manipulated unlockTime of User2 
User2 can no longer unlock at 100 sec, If Malicious User3 repeat this every time then User2 funds can be 
locked forever. 
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142


# Vulnerability details

## Description

The proposeUSDPrice function in the LockManager contract does not include a mechanism for proposal expiration. If other oracles do not vote for approval or disapproval, the proposal remains active indefinitely. This can block other functionalities, such as updating approval and disapproval thresholds using the setUSDThresholds function, which checks for an active proposal.

## Impact

- Stale Proposals: Proposals can remain active indefinitely if not enough votes are cast, leading to stale or outdated proposals.
- Blocked Functionality: Functions like setUSDThresholds cannot be executed if there is an active proposal, potentially blocking important updates.
- Operational Inefficiency: The inability to reset or expire proposals can lead to operational inefficiencies and hinder the contract's functionality.


## Proof of Concept

1. Create a Proposal:
        An oracle creates a new USD price proposal using proposeUSDPrice.
2. No Further Action:
        Other oracles do not vote for approval or disapproval, leaving the proposal in a pending state.
3. Blocked Threshold Update:
        Attempting to update the approval and disapproval thresholds using setUSDThresholds fails due to the active proposal check (if (usdUpdateProposal.proposer != address(0))).


## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Introduce a proposal expiration mechanism to ensure that proposals do not remain active indefinitely. This can be achieved by adding a deadline to the proposal and checking for expiration in relevant functions.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401-L410
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275-L294


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
A Normal User funds get locked in contract, beacuse each time an Malicious Attacker can frontrun User's `unlock()` Tx and lock some DUST amount on behalf him(User's behalf). In result `unlockTime` for Normal User increased and his `unlock()` Tx failed.

## Proof of Concept
So a user can unlock his locked fund via calling `unlock()` when `unlockTime` passed, below is the following code segment
```solidity

    function unlock(
        address _tokenContract,
        uint256 _quantity
    ) external notPaused nonReentrant {
        LockedToken storage lockedToken = lockedTokens[msg.sender][
            _tokenContract
        ];
        if (lockedToken.quantity < _quantity) 
            revert InsufficientLockAmountError();
        if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp)) //@audit
            revert TokenStillLockedError();
```
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L410-L412

But this protocol allow Any user to lock for another User via `lockOnBehalf()`

One major issue here is that there are no minimum amountchecks for `_quantity` locked

basically a User can call `lockOnBehalf() with DUST amount like 1wei` for another user's behalf & function flow will like below

`lockOnBehalf()  --> _lock()`
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275-L294

Whenever a lock happens following state change changes happen
```solidity
        lockedToken.remainder = remainder;
        lockedToken.quantity += _quantity;
        lockedToken.lastLockTime = uint32(block.timestamp);
        lockedToken.unlockTime =
            uint32(block.timestamp) +
            uint32(_lockDuration);
```
Here we see that with each lock, `unlockTime` set to `uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_lockDuration)`
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L382-L384

here `_lockDuration` could be `playerSettings[_lockRecipient].lockDuration` Or if this value not present then `lockdrop.minLockDuration`
```solidity
        uint32 _lockDuration = playerSettings[_lockRecipient].lockDuration;

        if (_lockDuration == 0) {
            _lockDuration = lockdrop.minLockDuration;
        }
```
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L347-L351

So With each DUST lock, `unlockTime` increased via `_lockDuration` period


By Following step this attack preformed
- A normal user `lock()` some fund
- when his `unlockTime` passed he wanted to withdraw his fund and call `unlock()`
- Malicious actor see this Tx,
- Malicious actor frontrun User's Tx, and call `lockOnBehalf()` with parameter `_quantity = 1wei(Dust)` & `_onBehalfOf = User's address`
- now `_lock()` get executed and stateVariables updated, so user's unlockTime now increased `block.timestamp + _lockDuration`
- User Tx (`unlock()`) failed due to below check
```solidity
        if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp))
            revert TokenStillLockedError();
```

This attack against a Regualr User can lunched multiple times, so basically that user will targeted by an attacker. By doing this an Attacker can keep locking User's fund for infinity time. 

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To prevent this `lockOnBehalf()` should have some sort of `minimum _quantity` check, so that it will become very expensive for an Attacker to keep locking User's fund.


## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L344-L387
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401-L424


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Nft could minted with DUST amount.

## Proof of Concept
While User call `unlock()` it on going to change `quantity` STATE variable but not consider `remainder`
```solidity
    function unlock(
        address _tokenContract,
        uint256 _quantity
    ) external notPaused nonReentrant {
        LockedToken storage lockedToken = lockedTokens[msg.sender][
            _tokenContract
        ];
        if (lockedToken.quantity < _quantity) // @audit Remainder not considered
            revert InsufficientLockAmountError();
        if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp))
            revert TokenStillLockedError();

        // force harvest to make sure that they get the schnibbles that they are entitled to
        accountManager.forceHarvest(msg.sender);

        lockedToken.quantity -= _quantity; // @audit-issue

        // send token
        if (_tokenContract == address(0)) {
            payable(msg.sender).transfer(_quantity); 
        } else {
            IERC20 token = IERC20(_tokenContract);
            token.transfer(msg.sender, _quantity); 
        }

        emit Unlocked(msg.sender, _tokenContract, _quantity);
    }
```
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401-L424

`unlock()` work as follows
- check `_quantity` parameter against `quantity` locked by this User
- Then adjust State of `quantity` corresponding to input parameter `_quantity`
- send corresponding amount to User

But Problem here is its not considering to reset or adjust `remainder` stored for that User

So a User can preform an attack and mint NFT with very less amount (Dust amount) due to above missing check.


### For Example :: 

> Assume a NFT cost = 1 eth

#### `Alice` call `lock()` with 0.9 ETH
> Quantity = 0.9 ETH
```solidity
       uint256 quantity = _quantity + lockedToken.remainder;
```
> remainder = 0.9 ETH
```solidity
       remainder = quantity % configuredToken.nftCost;
```
> No. Nft minted = 0
```soldity
        numberNFTs = (quantity - remainder) / configuredToken.nftCost;
```
So its STATES will be 
- remainder = 0.9 ETH
- quantity = 0.9 ETH (we are intersted in these 2. `remainder` & `quantity`)
- lastLockTime = block.timestamp
- unlockTime = block.timestamp + lockDuration
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L344-L387

In my [Previous Bug](https://code4rena.com/audits/2024-05-munchables/submit?issue=I_kwDOL-MQVM6KJAJS) Report i explained how this unlockTime could by passed, 
This attack can preform independently or also with addition of previos one. 


#### `Alice` call `unlock()` once `unlockTime` reached and withdraw all(0.9 ETH)
So its STATES will be 

- remainder = 0.9 ETH
- quantity = 0 ETH
...
...


#### `Alice` again call `lock()` with 0.1 Eth
> quantity = _quantity + lockedToken.remainder = 0.1 ETH + 0.9 ETH
> remainder = 0 ETH
> No. Nft minted = 1

So its STATES will be 
- remainder = 0 ETH
- quantity = 0.1 ETH 
- lastLockTime = block.timestamp
- unlockTime = block.timestamp + lockDuration

Here we can see Total locked fund for Alice is `0.1ETH` and 1 Nft minted for him.

This attack can also go beyond. An attacker can mint Nft with DUST amount by above approch. 

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
While `unlocking` for an user function should also accounted for `remainder` stored in storage

If fully unlocking happens then `remainder` should reset to 0
If partial then `remainder` adjusted with corresponding unlocking amount





## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L373-L377


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`WETH` Fund fetching by `_lock()` always revert due to special behaviour of `weth.transferFrom()` in BLAST.

## Proof of Concept
For locking token Users ca use `lock()` or `lockOnBehalf()` which 2 calls `_lock()` internally.
`_lock()` fetch caller funds via a `token.transferFrom()` & currently protocol is supporting 2 token `USDB` and `WETH`.
```solidity
        if (_tokenContract != address(0)) {
            IERC20 token = IERC20(_tokenContract); 
            token.transferFrom(_tokenOwner, address(this), _quantity); 
        }
```
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L373-L377

However, the transfer done using `address(weth).transferFrom`. This works fine on most chains (Ethereum, Optimism, Polygon, BSC) which uses the standard WETH9 contract that handles the case  when `src == msg.sender`:
```solidity
WETH9.sol
        if (src != msg.sender && allowance[src][msg.sender] != uint(- 1)) {
            require(allowance[src][msg.sender] >= wad);
            allowance[src][msg.sender] -= wad;
        }
```
The problem is that the WETH implementation on Blast uses [a different contract](https://blastscan.io/address/0x4300000000000000000000000000000000000004#code), and does not have this src == msg.sender handling.

Also, the issue is presented in [Wrapped Arbitrum](https://arbiscan.io/address/0x8b194beae1d3e0788a1a35173978001acdfba668#code) and  [Wrapped Fantom](https://ftmscan.com/token/0x21be370d5312f44cb42ce377bc9b8a0cef1a4c83#code).

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Try to use `trasfer()` instead of `transferFrom()`

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L256-L268


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users can change the lock duration to a shorter duration, which is unintended.

## Proof of Concept

Before changing the lock duration, it is checked that duration + block.timestamp >= unlockTime, This is so that the user can't set a duration that unlocks before the previous lock.
```solidity
// check they are not setting lock time before current unlocktime
 if (
     uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <
     lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime
 ) {
     revert LockDurationReducedError();
 }
```

But while updating the lock duration, `lastLockTime` instead of `block.timestamp` is used which makes the previous check ineffective.
```solidity

uint32 lastLockTime = lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract]
    .lastLockTime;
lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime =
    lastLockTime +
    uint32(_duration);
```

Example:
1. User creates a lock for a token, where unlockTime = 1000 and block.timestamp = 0 = lastLockTime 
2. Now block.timestamp is 500, User calls setLockDuration with duration = 501, the check will pass since (500 + 501 >= 1000), then the unlockTime will be set to
0 + 501 = 501
3. So user will be able to unlock in the next block


## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Use the below snippet [here](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L263-L267)

```solidity
lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime =
    block.timestamp +
    uint32(_duration);
```


## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L177-L242


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The price can be disapproved, but it's correct price which is intended to be approved by more than  APPROVE_THRESHOLD(=3)

## Proof of Concept
There are 5 roles to approve/disapprove the proposed price. 
If at least 3 roles approve or disapprove to assess the proposed price. Through inspect of approve, disapprove functions, approved user can't disapprove the price again, but user who did already disapprove can approve the price again.
So it means that user feels his previous disapproving decision is not correct, and changed his assessment result as approvement, but at this time, `usdUpdateProposal.disapprovals[msg.sender]` is not cleared and `disapprovalsCount` is not deducted according to it.
So it cause disapprovalsCount is remained unchanged. If another role disapproves the price, proposed price is not accepted as result.

ex:
role1 proposed price X -- approvalsCount = 1, disapprovalsCount = 0
role2 disapprove       -- approvalsCount = 1, disapprovalsCount = 1
role3 disapprove       -- approvalsCount = 1, disapprovalsCount = 2
role3 approve          -- approvalsCount = 2, disapprovalsCount = 2
role4 disapprove       -- approvalsCount = 2, disapprovalsCount = 3

Without role5's assessment, the price can be rejected.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
add the below checker in approve() function
```
        if (usdUpdateProposal.disapprovals[msg.sender] == _usdProposalId)
            revert ProposalAlreadyDisapprovedError();
```


## Assessed type

Other

    - Alice has successfully reducing her lock time by an additional 10 days

Players funds can get stuck in the lock manager without a way to withdraw as long as attacker decides.

## Proof of Concept
Anyone can call `lockOnBehalf(...)` to lock tokens on behalf of a registered player, however this is dangerous for player who already has a `_tokenContract` locked and moreso the attack path is cheap as the attacker only pays for gas

Assume time starts from t = day 0

```solidity

379:         lockedToken.remainder = remainder;

```

- Bob call `lockOnBehalf(...)` for Alice with 1 wei of token A,
- Alice who locked at t = day 30 could originally unlock on t = day 80 will not be able to unlock until t = day 90
- Bob can continue locking on behalf of Alice with dust amount every 10 days to extend Alice unlock time indefinitely
- He can increase the interval to make the attack cheaper

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
This can lead to 

- state variables are updated without the user actually making payment
- instances where are funds getting stuck and some players will not be able to withdraw sometimes

Per the [audit documentation](https://code4rena.com/audits/2024-05-munchables#toc-3-erc20-token-behaviors-in-scope)  tokens that do not revert on failure are in the scope of this audit.

## Proof of Concept
Some ERC20 Tokens do not revert on failure of the transfer function, but return a bool value instead. Some do not return any value. Therefore it is required to check if a value was returned, and if true, which value it is. This is not done on some places in these contracts.

When players lock their tokens with `lock(...)` function the player’s `lockedToken.quantity` is updated to include the amount tokens that the player entered.

However, if the the `tokenContract` is a token that does not revert on failure,

- the players `lockedToken.quantity` will be over inflated after locking if their transfer to `LockManager` fails.
- during unlocking, players can loose their funds if the transfer from the `LockManager` fails.

```solidity
File: LockManager.sol
373:         // Transfer erc tokens
374:         if (_tokenContract != address(0)) { // normal ERC not ETH
375:             IERC20 token = IERC20(_tokenContract);
376:  @>         token.transferFrom(_tokenOwner, address(this), _quantity);
377:         }
...
379:         lockedToken.remainder = remainder;
380:         lockedToken.quantity += _quantity;

```

- Alice locks 20_000e18 token A which is a token that does not revert on failure
- 20_000e18 transferred from Alice wallet to `LockManager` is not successful and balance of `LockManager` remains the same but `lockedToken.quantity` of Alice is increased by 20_000e18
- Bobs transfer of 20_000e18 goes through successfully
- Alice `unlock(...)` successfully
- Bob tries to `unlock(...)` but there not enough  tokens to settle him however his  `lockedToken.quantity` decreased but the transfer was unsuccessful
- Bob has lost his funds without any means of retrieval

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
- Check for the existence and value of the returned data of the `transferFrom(...)` call. If there is a return value, it has to be true. This could be achieved by using Openzeppelins SafeERC20 library´s `safeTransfer`.


## Assessed type

Token-Transfer

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275-L294
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L381-L387


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

_Griefing Attack:_
Lack of access control in `lockOnBehalf` function allows 
malicious users to lock the tokens of other players by repeatedly extending the `unlockTime`.

Impact: High
Likelihood : High

## Proof of Concept

Contract : LockManager 

As it stands 

`lockOnBehalf` function allows any `msg.sender` 
to lock tokens on behalf of another address `_onBehalfOf`,
which is the root cause of this attack.

The following example demonstrates the attack on a single user, executed one time.
But note that, 
this attack could be performed repeatedly on multiple player accounts.

Bob : Player/ victim
Alice : Attacker

_Step 1:_

Bob completes the registration and 
locks 5 WETH on May 1, 2024 ( block.timestamp = 1714521600) 

```
vm.startPrank(Bob);

lockManagerContract.lock(address(weth), 5 ether);

vm.stopPrank();
```


Going by the `minLockDuration` of 30 days

`lockedToken.unlockTime` for weth is set to May 30, 2024 (block.timestamp = 1717027200) 

`playerSettings[_lockRecipient].lockDuration` is set to `minLockDuration` = 30 days


_Step 2:_

Alice wants to keep Bob's funds locked in the contract 
to execute a griefing attack
or gain any potential advantage in game.  

On May 29, 2024 (block.timestamp = 1716940800)  

Alice calls the `lockOnBehalf` function with dust amount of weth
passing Bob's player account as the `lockRecipient`


```
vm.startPrank(Alice);

lockManagerContract.lockOnBehalf(
                    address(weth), 
                    1 wei, 
                    address(Bob)) 

vm.stopPrank();

```
Since `playerSettings[_lockRecipient].lockDuration` was set to 30 days.
The following line extends Bob's unlockTime till June 28, 2024.

```
lockedToken.unlockTime =
            uint32(block.timestamp) +
            uint32(_lockDuration);
```  


_Step 3:_        

Bob attempts to withdraw his weth funds on May 31st 

```
vm.startPrank(Bob);

vm.expectRevert();
lockManagerContract.unlock(address(weth), 5 ether);

vm.stopPrank();
```
and gets reverted with `TokenStillLockedError` 
due to the following check

```
if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp))
revert TokenStillLockedError();
```

Any user is able to execute this attack repeatedly, 
keeping other players' funds locked indefintely.


## Tools Used

Manual Review, Foundry


## Recommended Mitigation Steps

To prevent this, 
`lockOnBehalf` should require explicit consent from the `lockRecipient`. 

One way to implement this is by introducing an approval mechanism 
where users must approve another address to lock tokens on their behalf.

1. Add a mapping to store approvals

```
mapping(address => mapping(address => bool)) public lockOnBehalfApproval;
```

2. Add a function to allow users to approve another address:

```
function approveLockOnBehalf(address _approved) external {
    lockOnBehalfApproval[msg.sender][_approved] = true;
    emit ApprovalForLockOnBehalf(msg.sender, _spender);
}
```

3. Modify `lockOnBehalf` to check if the `msg.sender` is approved


With these changes, 
users can control who is allowed to lock tokens on their behalf, 
mitigating the risk of unauthorized extensions of the lock period.





## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L263-L267


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Likelihood : High
Impact : High

The following is one of the main invariants mentioned in the protocol documentation.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#attack-ideas-where-to-focus-for-bugs

```
people cannot reduce lockup times that are previously set
```

However, any user is able to exploit the following math error in `setLockDuration` function 
to unlock locked funds earlier than intended by the protocol.

```
lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime =
    lastLockTime + uint32(_duration);

```

This breaks the above mentioned invariant. 


## Proof of Concept

Contract : lockManager

This vulnerability stems from the way `unlockTime` is calculated in the `setLockDuration`

```
lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime =
    lastLockTime + uint32(_duration);

```

The above calculation of `unlockTime` takes into account 
the `lastLockTime` instead of using the `block.timestamp` value, 
which is the root cause of this issue.

Lets demonstrate with an example

Step 1: 

Bob locks 5 Ether of WETH tokens for the first time 
on 12 am, May 1, 2024 ( block.timestamp = 1714521600)

```
vm.startPrank(Bob);
lockManagerContract.lock ( address(weth), 5 ether )

```

`_lockDuration` is assigned a `minLockDuration` of 30 days.
such that 

`lastLockTime` = 12 am, May 1, 2024 ( block.timestamp = 1714521600)
`unlockTime` =  12 am, May 30, 2024 (block.timestamp = 1717027200)


Step 2: 

Bob waits till 1 am, May 16, 2024 ( block.timestamp = 1715821200)

Step 3 : 

Bob calls `setLockDuration` at 1 am, May 16th 2024 
with a `_duration` = 15 days,
inorder to avoid the following revert

```
                if (
                    uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <
                    lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime
                ) {
                    revert LockDurationReducedError();
                }
```

The `unlockTime ` is calculated as 

```
uint32 lastLockTime = 
    lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].lastLockTime;
        
lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime =
    lastLockTime + uint32(_duration);
```


1714521600 + 15 days =  1715817600 (12 am , May 16, 2024 ) 

which is clearly in the past. 


Step 4 : 

Bob immediately calls `unlock` and withdraws the WETH tokens 
much earlier than the minimum lock duration intended by the protocol

```
vm.startPrank(Bob);
lockManagerContract.unlock(address(weth), 5 ether);
```


## Tools Used

Manual Review, Foundry

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

To prevent this exploit, 
the new `unlockTime` should be calculated as 
the sum of current `block.timestamp` and `_duration`

`block.timestamp +  uint32(_duration) `

```

 if (lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].quantity > 0) {
            // Ensure new unlock time is in the future and greater than current unlock time
            uint32 newUnlockTime = uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration);

            lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime = newUnlockTime;
            
            if (newUnlockTime < lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime) {
                revert LockDurationReducedError();
            }
        }
        
```

As an additional measure,
check should be made after the update 
to ensure that the updated `unlockTime` remains larger than the previous unlockTime



## Assessed type

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L311-L398


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Impact : Medium
Likelihood : High

In the current implementation of the `_lock` function, 
subsequent calls to lock tokens for a user extend the `unlockTime` for all previously locked tokens. 

1. Inflexibility: 
Users cannot manage multiple lock periods. 
Each new lock extends the lock period for all tokens, which can be inconvenient.

2. Unintended Lock Extensions: 
Users might accidentally extend the lock period for previously locked tokens 
when they only intended to lock a new batch.


## Proof of Concept

NFT Cost : 1000 USDB

Bob chooses to lock USDB inorder to avoid the volatility of ETH

_Step 1 : Initial Lock to mint 10 NFTs_

  On April 1, 2024 12:00 PM  
  Bob locks 10,000 USDB with a lock duration of 30 days.

```
  unlockTime = April 30, 12:00 PM
  lockedToken.quantity = 1000
  lockedToken.unlockTime = April 30, 12:00 PM
```

_Step 2 : Subsequent Lock to mint 1 NFT_

  On April 25, 2024 12:00 PM 
  Bob locks an additional 1000 USDB with the same lock duration of 30 days.

  The `unlockTime` for all tokens, 
  including the previously locked 10,000 USDB got extended to May 25, 12:00 PM.


_Original Expectation:_
  Bob expected the first batch of 10000 tokens to be unlocked on April 30.

_Reality:_ 
  Due to the subsequent lock, 
  the unlock time for all 11000 USDB tokens is now extended to May 25, 12:00 PM.

_Inflexibility:_ 
  Bob cannot manage multiple lock periods for different batches of tokens. 
  Each new lock extends the lock period for all previously locked tokens, 
  leading to unintentional delays in accessing his initially locked tokens.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Here’s a possible approach to improve this:

1. Introduce a Struct for Each Batch: 
Create a struct to store information about each batch of locked tokens.

```
struct LockedTokenBatch {
    uint256 quantity;
    uint32 lockTime;
    uint32 unlockTime;
}

```


2. Track Batches for Each User: 
Use a mapping to store an array of LockedTokenBatch for each user and token contract.

```
mapping(address => mapping(address => LockedTokenBatch[])) public lockedTokenBatches;

```

3. Update _lock Function: 
   Modify the _lock function to create a new batch each time tokens are locked.

4. Update unlock Function: 
   Modify the unlock function to handle unlocking specific batches.

#Benefits of the Fix

_Flexibility:_ 
  Users can manage multiple batches of locked tokens, each with its own lock 
  period.

_Clarity:_ 
  Lock and unlock operations are clearer, 
  as each batch is treated independently.

_Fairness:_ 
  Users are not unintentionally affected by subsequent lock operations.
  This approach ensures that each locking operation is independent, 
  allowing users to lock and unlock their tokens with greater flexibility and 
  control.





## Assessed type

DoS

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

In the current `_lock` function implementation, 
tokens locked outside the lockdrop period are not added to the `lockedToken.remainder`, 
which means they are not considered for minting NFTs when the next lockdrop period opens. 

This creates a discrepancy for users who lock tokens outside the lockdrop period 
and expect them to count towards NFT minting in future lockdrop periods.

Impact : Medium
Likelihood : High

## Proof of Concept

_Tokens Locked Outside Lockdrop Period: _

NFT Cost : 2000 USDB


_1. First Lock (Outside Lockdrop Period)_

-- Bob locks 1900 tokens on  March 29th 
-- lockupDuration : 60 days
-- These tokens are not added to the remainder for NFT minting


_2. Second Lock (Within Lockdrop Period) _
 (lockdrop period is announced to be open from April 1 to April 30)

-- Bob locks 100 tokens on April 2nd
-- Only these 100 tokens are added to remainder and considered for NFT minting, 
   and Bob misses out on potentially minting 1 NFT for the previously locked 1900 tokens.

## Tools Used

Manual Review, Foundry

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Modify the `_lock` function to account for 
tokens locked outside the lockdrop period and add them to the remainder.
This ensures they are considered for minting NFTs when the next lockdrop period opens.


## Assessed type

Other

# Vulnerability details

In the setLockDuration function, when the user updates the lock duration, the new unlockTime is required to be longer than the original unlockTime, so for https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/ The code of managers/LockManager.sol#L257 requires that the current time plus _duration be greater than the original unlockTime, which means that the new unlockTime is calculated based on the current time. But when the code at https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L265 updates unlockTime, it updates according to lastLockTime, and lastLockTime is the user The time the lock was created. So there is obviously an error here, because block.timestamp is greater than lastLockTime, then the user can update unlockTime with a smaller _duration, causing the lock to be released early.

Math

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L244-L272
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L256-L261
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L263-L267


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
This report identifies a vulnerability in the lockup functionality of the `lockedTokens` contract. The current implementation allows users to potentially reduce their previously set lockup duration. 
Based on the attack ideas given by the sponsor, a user should not be allowed to set the unlocktime below the previous time.
https://code4rena.com/audits/2024-05-munchables#top:~:text=and%20that%20people%20cannot%20reduce%20lockup%20times%20that%20are%20previously%20set.


## Proof of Concept

The code snippet responsible for lockup extension appears to have a flaw:

```solidity
if (uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) < lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime) {
  revert LockDurationReducedError();
}
```

This check compares the sum of the current timestamp and the new `_duration` with the existing `unlockTime`. It aims to prevent reducing the lockup period.

**Impact:**

However, the code doesn't consider the `lastLockTime`. Here's how an attacker could exploit this:

1. Set initial lockup duration (`_duration`) to a high value (e.g., 800 seconds).
2. The `unlockTime` gets set based on the current timestamp and `_duration`.
3. Later, the attacker calls the function again with a shorter `_duration`. The check passes because the sum of the current timestamp and the new `_duration` might be less than the existing `unlockTime`.
4. However, the actual lockup duration gets reduced because the `unlockTime` is updated based on the `lastLockTime` and the new `_duration`.


 for example 

let's say 
former duration is set at 1000 .
new duration is set at 800 .
200 seconds have passed.
at the current time stamp is 212000,
the former unlocktime is 212800, 
lastLockTime is 211800. 

 based on the above 

```solidity
if (uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) < lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime) {
  revert LockDurationReducedError();
}
```
212000+800 will pass. but  


```solidity

uint32 lastLockTime = lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract]
                    .lastLockTime;
lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime =
                    lastLockTime +
                    uint32(_duration);

```
 The new unlocktime = 211800+800=212600 this is lesser than the previous unlock time 212800.

## Tool 

Manual Code analysis

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

- Replace the check with one that directly compares the new `_duration` with the difference between the current `unlockTime` and the `lastLockTime`:

```solidity
if (_duration < lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime - uint32(lastLockTime)) {
  revert LockDurationReducedError();
}
```
or 
 Instead set unlock time based on the former check.
```solidity
lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime =
                    uint32(block.timestamp) +
                    uint32(_duration);

```



## Assessed type

Error

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L460-L487
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L472-L482


# Vulnerability details


## Impact

A potential overflow can occur in the calculation of `lockedWeighted`, which can cause the _lockedWeightedValue of some tokens to always revert. Looking at the code implemented

LockManager line 472  // We are assuming all tokens have a maximum of 18 decimals and that USD Price is denoted in 1e18. 

BUT Implementing 1e18 has the maximum goes against the README.

https://code4rena.com/audits/2024-05-munchables#top:~:text=High%20decimals%20(%20%3E%2018,Yes
ALSO Note other token can be added in the future 
https://code4rena.com/audits/2024-05-munchables#top:~:text=USDB%2C%20WETH%2C%20(assume%20we%20can%20add%20more%20to%20the%20future%20for%20use%20in%20LockManager).
AS stated in the link tokens above decimal 18 are in scope, hence this will lead to a revertion if such tokens are ever added.

## Proof of Concept

The following code snippet demonstrates the potential overflow:

```solidity
uint256 deltaDecimal = 10 ** (18 - configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals);
lockedWeighted += (deltaDecimal * lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]].quantity * configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].usdPrice) / 1e18;
```

The issue lies in the calculation of `deltaDecimal`. If `configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals` is greater than 18, the subtraction results in a negative exponent for `10**`. This negative exponent can lead to unexpected behavior or overflows during the multiplication. Therefore the transaction automatically reverts.



## Tools Used

Manual Code analysis

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

1. **Support Decimals Above 18:**

   ```solidity
   uint256 deltaDecimal = configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals > 18 ?
       1e18 ** (configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals - 18) :
       10 ** (18 - configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals);
   ```

   This approach uses exponentiation with `1e18` for decimals above 18, avoiding negative exponents and potential overflows.

2. **Restrict Token Addition:**

   - Implement a mechanism to restrict adding new tokens to those with decimals less than or equal to 18 during token registration.
   - Clearly document and communicate this restriction to users.







## Assessed type

Under/Overflow

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L157-L158


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Token prices may be maliciously delayed, resulting in erroneous prices.

## Proof of Concept
In the contract, the price of the token is determined based on proposals and votes initiated by 5 PriceFeeds. And [only one price proposal can exist at the same time](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L157-L158). Therefore, if there is a PriceFeed that continuously initiates proposals with wrong prices, proposals with correct prices cannot be initiated, and price updates will be delayed.

## Tools Used

manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It is recommended to obtain the price of chainlink. If the price is not updated after a certain period of time, the effective price of chainlink shall prevail.





## Assessed type

Oracle

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users may lose part of the remainder funds.

## Proof of Concept
remainder represents the non-divisible part of the user's pledge, and quantity represents the divisible part of the user's pledge.

If the user locks during the lockdrop, and the remainder is not equal to 0. After the lockdrop ends, and the user locks again, [the contract will directly set the remainder to 0, and will not add the previous remainder to the quantity](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L379-L380). In this way, the user loses the remainder of locks.

```solidity
        uint256 quantity = _quantity + lockedToken.remainder;
        uint256 remainder;
···
        lockedToken.remainder = remainder;
        lockedToken.quantity += _quantity;
```

## Tools Used
manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Remainder should be calculated correctly even if addReveal is not called.





## Assessed type

Math

title: Inability to execute `_execUSDPriceUpdate` due to deletion of `usdUpdateProposal` array in `proposeUSDPrice` Function.
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L161
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L202


# Vulnerability details

The `proposeUSDPrice` function initiates a new proposal that can be approved or disapproved. When a proposal is approved the `approvalsCount` increments, when disapproved the `disapprovalsCount` increments. However, each new proposal triggers the deletion of the `usdUpdateProposal` struct, which tracks these counts. Consequently, `approvalsCount` and `disapprovalsCount` are reset to zero with each new proposal, preventing them from reaching the `APPROVE_THRESHOLD` or `DISAPPROVE_THRESHOLD` needed for execution.

## Impact
Cause the `approvalsCount` will never reach the `APPROVE_THRESHOLD`.

```javascript
 if (usdUpdateProposal.approvalsCount >= APPROVE_THRESHOLD) {
     _execUSDPriceUpdate();
        }
```

The `_execUSDPriceUpdate()` will never execute thus configuredTokens usd price will not update.

## Proof of Concept

Let's assume a process for updating the USD price for configured tokens:

1) `Role.PriceFeed_1` initiates a proposal.
2) The proposal is approved by `Role.PriceFeed_2`.
3) Now the `usdUpdateProposal.approvalsCount` = 2.
4) `Role.PriceFeed_1` initiates a new proposal.
5) This new proposal deletes the usdUpdateProposal struct, resetting `usdUpdateProposal.approvalsCount` to 0.
6) The new proposal is approved by `Role.PriceFeed_2`.
7) Now still the `usdUpdateProposal.approvalsCount = 2`, which should be 4 because two proposals have been approved.
8) Thus, the `usdUpdateProposal.approvalsCount` will never exceed 2 and usd price will not update.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L382


# Vulnerability details

The `lock` function is responsible for locking a user's tokens for a specified `_duaration`. Where users can only unlock their tokens once their `unlockTime` has elapsed. However, the `LockManager.sol` contract includes a `lockOnBehalf` function, which allows any user to lock tokens on behalf of another user.

Now a malicious user or attacker can exploit the `lockOnBehalf` function. By locking same tokens with a `0 quantity ` on behalf of another user, and can repeatedly extend their `unlockTime`.

## Impact

Denial of Service (DoS) Attack: Bob, the attacker, can continuously extend the `unlockTime` of Alice's tokens, preventing her from unlocking her funds as intended.

```javascript
 if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp))
            revert TokenStillLockedError();
```

## Proof of Concept

Scenario:

1. Let's assume a user, Alice, locks 10 WETH tokens with a default `_lockduration` of 30 days.
```javascript
if (_lockDuration == 0) {
  _lockDuration = lockdrop.minLockDuration;
}
```

2. Alice's `unlockTime` is calculated as follows:
```javascript
lockedToken.unlockTime = uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_lockDuration);
```

3. After 10 days, an attacker, Bob, maliciously locks 0 tokens for Alice via `lockOnBehalf` function.

4. Consequently, Alice's unlock time gets extended by 10 days, as her lock time is reset by Bob's action.

5. Bob can repeat this process.

## Tools Used
Manual review.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Consider implementing minimum and maximum limits for tokens that can be locked by users in `_lock` function.
Or restrict access to the `lockOnBehalf` function to authorized users only.


## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L380


# Vulnerability details

The `lock` function is responsible for locking the user's tokens for a particular `_duration`. However, the `_lock` function adds the previous `remainder` each time when a user locks the token again to his provided `quantity`.

```javascript
uint256 quantity = _quantity + lockedToken.remainder;
```

And also adds whole provided `quantity` to user to `unlock` at a particular `unlockTime`.

```javascript
lockedToken.quantity += _quantity;
```

So the problem is here that a user can `unlock` the entire provided `quantity` after first `lock`, along with the previous `remainder` amount, during their second locking action.


## Impact
As much as `configuredToken.nftCost` grows user will be able to steal more tokens according to below statement:

The highest remainder can be calculated as:
`nftCost - 1`

## Proof of Concept
Scenario:

1) Let's say the user locks `199` tokens which nftCost = `100`.
2) Now remainder will be `99` according to this:

   ```javascript
   remainder = quantity % configuredToken.nftCost;
   ```

3) So, due to the below statements in the `_lock` function, that users are able to unlock all the provided tokens, 
   after the `unlockTime` finishes.

   ```javascript
   lockedToken.quantity += _quantity
   ```

4) User unlocks `199` when the `unlockTime` elapsed.
5) After that, the user again locks `1` more token, and since the `remainder` is now `99`, the `quantity` will be  
   `100` according to the below statement.

   ```javascript
     uint256 quantity = _quantity + lockedToken.remainder;
   ```

6) He Waits until the `unlockTime` finishes, call the `unlock` function again, and gather `100` more tokens.
7) In this way, the user drains `99` tokens.

## Tools Used
Manual review.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider implement this on `unlock` function.

```diff
+   lockedToken.quantity += _quantity - remainder;
```



## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L177-L207


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
For a proposal to be executed, it must receive sufficient approvals. On the other hand, the proposal could be disapproved. Only Role.PriceFeed can approve and disapprove. In the current implementation, it seems that they are limited to not giving more than one vote, but there is a way to make double voting possible.
Role.PriceFeed can first disapprove and then approve, which can compromise the whole logic of the vote due to the possibility of giving 2 votes rather than the expected 1.  

## Proof of Concept

Lets say we have the following scenario:
APPROVE_THRESHOLD=3; 
DISAPPROVE_THRESHOLD=3;

1.A proposal is submitted and awaits approval
2.Role.PriceFeed_1 disapproves the proposal //0 approvals - 1 disapproval
3.Role.PriceFeed_2 approves the proposal // 1 approval - 1 disapproval
4.Role.PriceFeed_3 approves the proposal // 2 approvals - 1 disapproval
5.Role.PriceFeed_4 disapproves the proposal // 2 approvals - 2 disapprovals
6.Role.PriceFeed_1 approves the proposal // 3 approval - 2 disapprovals

The proposal will be executed based on Role.PriceFeed_1 double voting (2,6).


## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider removing the possibility for double voting. In approveUSDPrice() add:
```
if (usdUpdateProposal.disapprovals[msg.sender] == _usdProposalId)
            revert ProposalAlreadyDisapprovedError();
```


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L129-L139


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
APPROVE_THRESHOLD and DISAPPROVE_THRESHOLD are used in proposal functionality of the protocol. They can be changed from admin  in setUSDThresholds(). In approveUSDPrice() and disapproveUSDPrice() new proposal USD price is approved based on those thresholds. Currently they are set to 3 and this is legit based on the fact that the votes that could be received are 5. (Role.PriceFeed_1 ... Role.PriceFeed_5). The problem is that admin can set those thresholds too high by mistake or maliciously. In this case the whole proposal logic could be stuck if the required approvals and disapprovals are much more than the possible votes. Also then the admin will be not able to set new thresholds, because in setUSDThresholds() we have this check:
```
 if (usdUpdateProposal.proposer != address(0))
            revert ProposalInProgressError();
```
It will revert because of the fact that there is a proposal that is stuck. This means that no new proposals will be possible and the USD price will never change.

## Proof of Concept
1.Lets say we have Role.PriceFeed_1 ... Role.PriceFeed_5. This means we have 5 possible votes.
2.Admin set APPROVE_THRESHOLD=6 and DISAPPROVE_THRESHOLD=6
3.Proposal is created and the approval process is going.
4.All votes are approves for this proposal, but 5<6 so the proposal cannot be approved and gets stuck
5.New APPROVE_THRESHOLD and DISAPPROVE_THRESHOLD cannot be set because proposal is in progress.

In this scenario the USD price cannot be changed.
Keep in mind that the proposal will be stuck in any of the possible votes scenarios with thresholds higher than the count of possible votes.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To enhance safety and reliability, introduce a range of appropriate approval and disapproval thresholds in setUSDThresholds(). 


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L98-L112
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L311-L398
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L245-L272


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The vulnerability in the configureLockdrop() function allows the admin to set lockdrop.minLockDuration without proper validation. This missing validation can result in minLockDuration being set to 0 or an excessively large value. Such misconfigurations can severely impact the locking mechanism in the following ways:

```
if (_lockDuration == 0) {
    _lockDuration = lockdrop.minLockDuration;
        }
```

1.Lock Duration Too Short (0): If lockdrop.minLockDuration is set to 0, the _lock function's internal check for a 0 _lockDuration will result in the _lockDuration being set to lockdrop.minLockDuration, which is also 0. This renders the lock functionality meaningless because the intended minimum lock duration is bypassed, allowing immediate unlocking.

2.Lock Duration Excessively Long: If lockdrop.minLockDuration is set to an value bigger than ```uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))```, any attempt to lock tokens would result in revert.

```
if (
             _lockDuration < lockdrop.minLockDuration ||
                _lockDuration >
                uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))
            ) revert InvalidLockDurationError();
```


## PoC
Case 1
1.lockdrop.minLockDuration is set to 0 by mistake or maliciously.
2.playerSettings[_lockRecipient].lockDuration is 0.
3._lockDuration will be set to 0.

User will not be able to lock, because lock period will be 0.

Case 2
1.lockdrop.minLockDuration is set to bigger than uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration)) by mistake or maliciously.
2.playerSettings[_lockRecipient].lockDuration is 0.
3._lockDuration will be set to bigger than uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))
 
_lock() will revert because of:
```
if (
            _lockDuration < lockdrop.minLockDuration ||
                _lockDuration >
                uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))
            ) revert InvalidLockDurationError();
```
Case 3

1.lockdrop.minLockDuration is set to a value greater than uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration)) either by mistake or maliciously.
2.If a player sets their lock duration (playerSettings[_lockRecipient].lockDuration) to 15 for example.
This value is considered as a validated because: 
```
 function setLockDuration(uint256 _duration) external notPaused {
        if (_duration > configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))
            revert MaximumLockDurationError();
```
The lock operation will revert because the player's lock duration (15) is less than the excessively large lockdrop.minLockDuration.

```
if (
            _lockDuration < lockdrop.minLockDuration ||
                _lockDuration >
                uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))
            ) revert InvalidLockDurationError();
```

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To mitigate this vulnerability, add validation checks in the configureLockdrop() function to ensure that minLockDuration is within a reasonable and expected range. For instance, setting a minimum and maximum threshold for minLockDuration can prevent it from being set to an inappropriate value.



## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L245


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Some configuredTokenContracts will not be able to update `unlockTime` when `setLockDuration` gets called.

## Proof of Concept
[setLockDuration](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L245) is updating [unlockTime](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L265) for configuredTokenContracts array according to `_duration` which seems fine, until a revert is done at [L260](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L260-L261):

```
	if (
			uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <
			lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime
		) {
			revert LockDurationReducedError();
		}
```

This condition will revert if `unlockTime` greater than _duration + block.timestamp, which is a check must be done to make sure that _duration doesn't cross `unlockTime` time.

This revert will block other lockedTokens from able to update `unlockTime` since they don't violate this check above.

Example:
- we have Tokens A,B,C of lockedTokens.
- A does violate the check:
```
uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <
			lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime
```
- B doesn't and C doesn't.
- the user can't update `unlockTime` for tokens B and C since a revert is done for token A.
- put in mind that users would like to invest in different tokens with different unlock period of time for each token.

You could assume that by changing [_duration](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L245) the issue is solved, but actually is not, because users could decide to have different unlockTime for each token, and they should be able to pass their _duration differently with each token, but in our case they will be blocked.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Enable the user to pass array of configuredTokenContracts instead of looping on all of it.


## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L414


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
unlock with partial quantity will reset the last harvest time in account manager.
So, the user will lose rewards ...etc.

## Proof of Concept
forceHarvest at [accountManager.forceHarvest(msg.sender)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L414) can be an issue since it updates [lastHarvestDate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L382) to the current block.timestamp.

A user called [unlock](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401) with partial `_quantity`, a `forceHarvest` is done at:
```
accountManager.forceHarvest(msg.sender);
```
and now all the rewards harvested according to [secondsToClaim](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L376), which is:
```
block.timestamp - players[_caller].lastHarvestDate
```
The issue here when a user try to claim the remaining of lockedToken.quantity, there will be no harvest rewards for it, and users now need to wait for a period of time so they can harvest rewards for the remining quantity.

Assuming Bob has lockedToken.quantity = 100e18.
- Bob calls [unlock](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401) for _quantity as 10e18.
- A forceHarvest is done for 10e18 according to [secondsToClaim](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L376)
- [lastHarvestDate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L382) now is updated to the current block.timestamp.
- Bob calls `unlock` again for the remaining _quantity as 90e18, but doesn't harvest any rewards, since forceHarvest relys on `lastHarvestDate`.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Pass _quantity to  `forceHarvest` method and update the code.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
unlock can deliver incorrect rewards amounts or more than expected, because of lockedToken.quantity.

## Proof of Concept
[unlock](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401) method is decreasing the _quantity after a harvest is done.
```
accountManager.forceHarvest(msg.sender);

lockedToken.quantity -= _quantity;
```
let's explore the flow  of forceHarvest. -> means a call is done:
[forceHarvest](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L414) -> [_harvest](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L372) -> [getDailySchnibbles](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L373) -> [getLockedWeightedValue](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L366).

Above we can see that `forceHarvest` is relying on _lockedWeightedValue that returned from [getLockedWeightedValue](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L461), the issue here is when lockedWeighted gets calculated relying on [quantity](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L479).
```
lockedWeighted +=
		(deltaDecimal *
			lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]]
				.quantity *
			configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]]
				.usdPrice) /
		1e18;
```

let's get back again to `unlock` method, is being called before decreasing the _quantity at [L414](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L414), meaning in `getLockedWeightedValue` is being called before decreasing or updating `lockedToken.quantity`, let's put this in mind for the next scenario:
- Alex has of lockedToken.quantity as 10e18.
- Alex called unlock for 1e18 _quantity amount.
- forceHarvest will be done and call getLockedWeightedValue.
- `getLockedWeightedValue` will calculate `lockedWeighted` according to current [quantity](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L479) which is 100e18 at the moment (no decrease done yet).
- Alex can keep calling for low partial amounts (_quantity), and harvest more than it should be, since the decrease `lockedToken.quantity -= _quantity`[L416](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L416) is happening after forceHarvest.

This behavior would be problematic and cause incorrect `getLockedWeightedValue` very time that a user calls unlock method for partial _quantity.

The issue arise when one can keep calling unlock for low amounts and make unlock calculated rewards for old quantity every time, assuming we have 100e18 quantity:
- unlock for 10e18 _quantity -> getLockedWeightedValue calculate `lockedWeighted` for 100e18.
- again unlock for 10e18 _quantity -> getLockedWeightedValue calculate `lockedWeighted` for 90e18.
- again unlock for 10e18 _quantity -> getLockedWeightedValue calculate `lockedWeighted` for 70e18 and so on...


## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
- The decrease of quantity should be done before `forceHarvest`.
- Calculations for lockedWeighted at `getLockedWeightedValue` should be done on the requested partial _quantity of unlock, not the remaning value of lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]].quantity.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Some amounts of USDB might be locked forever in the protocol. In other cases, insolvency could be possible, meaning, the last user might not be able to unlock their full amount. 

## Proof of Concept
USDB on Blast is a rebase token, so the balance can change at any time.
The mechanism behind rebase tokens is altering the token supply proportionally across all existing holders' balances. 

When the token's price deviates from its target, a rebase event is triggered, where in the protocol adjusts the token supply by either increasing or decreasing the number of tokens each user holds. this adjustment aims to push the token's price toward its intended target, stabilizing its value over time.

The issue could happen when some USDB amounts are used in the protocol to be locked, since the lock duration can be up to 90 days, it is possible for the USDB rebase token amount to be changed. Therefore, the balance of LockManager contract might change. 

This would lead to a simple conclusion: big deposits of USDB can decrease or increase with the time while they are being locked, thus incase the amount of X increased, the user will lose the increasing value since he can only claim those stored at the time of locking. These surplus amounts can not be recovered by the protocol as there is no method to do so.

Moreover, if the balance in the contract decreased instead, the last user to unlock their USDB will incur loss, unlike early users who can unlock their full amounts of USDB.



## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Use a wrapper for the rebase token USDB (or any other rebase token that will be used) to behave as a standard ERC20 token

Other

The detailed description of the impact of the identified issue in the provided code revolves around potential smart contract configuration and security risks associated with blockchain deployment scripts. Here's a breakdown of the impacts:

Smart Contract Configuration Risks
Incorrect Addresses and Roles: The script configures various smart contracts and assigns roles to them. Incorrect addresses or roles assigned could lead to failed transactions or unauthorized access to contract functionalities. This misconfiguration could disrupt the intended workflow of the blockchain application, affecting its functionality and security.
Lack of Flexibility in Configuration: The script hardcodes many values and configurations, reducing flexibility. Changes to the blockchain network, smart contracts, or business requirements would necessitate modifications to the script, increasing the maintenance burden and potential for errors.
Security Risks
Reentrancy Attacks: The script interacts with smart contracts, which could be vulnerable to reentrancy attacks if not properly protected. Reentrancy allows an attacker to repeatedly call a function before the first call is finished, potentially draining funds or manipulating contract states.
Front-Running: Transactions broadcasted to the network can be seen by miners and potentially manipulated by malicious actors who can see pending transactions. This could lead to front-running attacks, where attackers submit similar transactions with higher fees to execute before the original transaction.
Insufficient Access Controls: The script sets up roles and permissions for various entities. Weak or improperly implemented access controls could allow unauthorized users to perform actions they shouldn't, compromising the integrity and security of the blockchain application.
Operational Impacts
Increased Gas Costs: The script performs numerous write operations to the blockchain, which are costly in terms of gas. High gas costs can increase operational expenses and may deter users from performing certain actions.
Potential for Silent Failures: The script's reliance on asynchronous operations and error handling could lead to silent failures, where errors occur but are not adequately logged or handled, leading to undetected issues that could affect the application's performance or availability.
Maintenance and Testing Challenges
Complexity and Debugging Difficulty: The script's complexity, especially regarding smart contract interactions and asynchronous operations, increases the difficulty of debugging and maintaining the code. This complexity also makes it harder to test thoroughly, potentially missing edge cases or vulnerabilities.
Dependence on External Libraries and Modules: The script depends on external libraries and modules, introducing dependency management challenges. Outdated or incompatible versions could introduce bugs or security vulnerabilities, requiring careful version management and compatibility checks.

Addressing these risks requires careful review, testing, and adherence to best practices in smart contract development and blockchain application design.
