# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L410


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
user can unlocked token in the same unlock time due to the operator used to check against current block.timestamp.

## Proof of Concept
unlock function is used to unlock some or whole quantity of the locked token and transfer it to the user, the issue in this function is that the locked tokens can be unlocked at the same exact unlocked time that shouldn't be the case.
Locked token can only be unlocked after successfully passing the unlock time.
```solidity
LockManager.sol#L410
if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp))
            revert TokenStillLockedError();
```
AS we can see above if statement only checks if the unlock time is greater then  block.timestamp, for example suppose a user wants to unlock their locked token and lets assume the unlock time is 1716609517 and the block.timestamp is also 1716609517, the if statement will not revert instead it will unlock the token and transferred it to the user that should not be the case it should make a revert when current and unlock timestamp are same because unlock time not passed its in the range.

## Tools Used
Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make the required changes as,
```diff
-    if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp))
            revert TokenStillLockedError();
+    if (lockedToken.unlockTime >= uint32(block.timestamp))
            revert TokenStillLockedError();
```

Context

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L177-L179


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
if the PriceFeed's transaction takes a long time in the mempool, then another prop node for another token with the same price may be approved, which was not originally intended.

## Proof of Concept
Function approveUSDPrice dont have parameter _usdProposalId, only _price. So, if priceFeed's tx is in mempool too long, the old proposal (for which the approval was intended) was deleted (it was accepted or rejected - it doesn’t matter), and at the moment another proposal is already active, with the same price, but for a different token. The price feeder may not agree with this price for another token, but the transaction will be accepted and his vote will be counted.
Explain:
1. PriceFeed1 call proposeUSDPrice(price:1000, _contracts:0x123,0x456)
2. PriceFeed2 agree with this price and call approveUSDPrice(1000), but this tx there is too long in mempool and still didnt included in the block.
3. Other priceFeeds accounts approve this price and proposal has executed and deleted.
4. PriceFeed1 call proposeUSDPrice(price:1000, _contracts:0x789) // <-- another contract!
5. PriceFeed2's tx (from step 2) has executed and new proposal now has approve from priceFeed2, but was intended for another proposal. 

Also, accounts with priceFeeed roles, could not revoke his votes.
The same situation with function disapproveUSDPrice.
## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add parameter address[] _contracts or uint32 _usdProposalId in approveUSDPrice() and disapproveUSDPrice()


## Assessed type

Oracle

raw_row.title: When user unlock all tokens, remainder value does not delete

title: When user unlock all tokens, remainder value does not delete
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L416


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
When user lock tokens, and execute calculation count of nfts, some value could be write into remainder value. But after unlockTime, user can call unlock() and get all tokens back, but remainder value does not delete, so in next call to lock() function, he could use less tokens, than it needed, because will be uses specified quantity and remainder value from previous lock.

## Proof of Concept
Example:
configuredToken.nftCost = 3;
User call lock(10) -> quantity=10, remainder=1 (10%3=1)
```solidity
function lock() {
   ....
   remainder = quantity % configuredToken.nftCost;
   numberNFTs = (quantity - remainder) / configuredToken.nftCost;
   ...
   lockedToken.remainder = remainder; // 1
   lockedToken.quantity += _quantity; // 3
```
When block.timestamp will be > unlockTime, user call unlock(10).
```solidity
function unlock() {
   ...
   lockedToken.quantity -= _quantity;
   // But dont set 0 in remainder value.
```
User call lock(8) 
```solidity
function lock() {
   ...
   uint256 quantity = _quantity + lockedToken.remainder;  // 8 + 1= 9
   ...
   remainder = quantity % configuredToken.nftCost; // 9%3=0
   numberNFTs = (quantity - remainder) / configuredToken.nftCost; // (9-0) / 3=3
```
So, user use less tokens in second call of lock, than in first call.
## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
```diff
   function unlock() {
   ...
   lockedToken.quantity -= _quantity;
+  lockedToken.remainder = 0;
```


## Assessed type

Other

raw_row.title: Improper Handling of Token Decimal Precision in `LockManager` Contract

title: Improper Handling of Token Decimal Precision in `LockManager` Contract
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L297-L371


# Vulnerability details

## Vulnerability Detail
In the `LockManager` contract, the calculation of the locked token value and the issuance of rewards (like NFTs) depend on the precision (decimals) of the token being locked. The contract does not correctly handle tokens with different decimal places, which will lead to incorrect calculations, allowing users to exploit the system to gain an unfair advantage or causing under/overestimation of locked values.
Also, the number of NFTs issued is calculated based on the `nftCost` parameter, which assumes a standard decimal format. If a token with fewer decimals is used, the calculation may result in fewer NFTs being issued than intended, or if more decimals are used, more NFTs than intended.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L381-L384


# Vulnerability details

While this check
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L356-L360
```solidity
if (
    _lockDuration < lockdrop.minLockDuration ||
    _lockDuration > uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))
) revert InvalidLockDurationError();
```

ensures that the lock duration for any single lock operation is within the minimum and maximum bounds, it does not prevent the cumulative lock duration from exceeding the maximum limit when multiple locks are performed consecutively.

## Impact
The current lock mechanism allows the lock duration to extend beyond the maximum allowed period (90 days) if a user repeatedly locks additional tokens before the previous lock expires. This circumvents the intended limit on the maximum lock duration and enables users to unfairly receive bonus rewards for extended periods.

## Proof of Concept
The `_lock` function resets the `lastLockTime` and recalculates the `unlockTime` each time tokens are locked:
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L381-L384
```solidity
lockedToken.lastLockTime = uint32(block.timestamp);
lockedToken.unlockTime = uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_lockDuration);
```
By resetting `lastLockTime` to the current block timestamp and setting `unlockTime` to the current timestamp plus the lock duration, the effective lock period can be extended indefinitely with repeated locks. This allows users to circumvent the intended maximum lock duration.

Initial Lock:User locks tokens for 70 days.
Subsequent Lock:On the 69th day, the user locks more tokens.
Result: Unlock time is recalculated to the current time + 70 days, effectively resulting in a lock period of 139 days from the initial lock.

The total effective lock period now exceeds the maximum intended duration of 90 days.

## Tools Used
Manual  Review.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To ensure the lock duration never exceeds the maximum allowed duration, we should modify the logic to respect the maximum lock duration limit by checking the total cumulative lock duration.

```solidity
uint32 maxLockDuration = uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration));
uint32 newUnlockTime = uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_lockDuration);

if (newUnlockTime > lockedToken.lastLockTime + maxLockDuration) {
    revert MaximumLockDurationExceededError();
}

lockedToken.unlockTime = newUnlockTime;
```

# Vulnerability details



## Description

The `LockManager` contract is designed to lock ERC20 tokens. One of these tokens, USDB, is implemented using the `ERC20Rebasing` contract, which supports different yield modes and automatic rebasing. The lock mechanism in `LockManager` may not correctly account for the accrued yields resulting from the rebasing of USDB. Consequently, the yield accrued due to automatic rebasing can be lost, as it cannot be properly claimed or reflected in the locked amounts.



## Impact

- **Loss of Accrued Yield:** The primary adverse outcome is that any yield accrued due to automatic rebasing may be lost, as `LockManager` does not account for these changes. Users will not be able to claim the additional tokens generated through rebasing, potentially resulting in significant financial loss over time.



## Proof of Concept



### Locking USDB:

```solidity

// User locks 1000 USDB

lockManager.lock(tokenAddress, 1000 * 10**18);

```



### Rebasing Event:

Assume USDB undergoes a rebasing event, increasing the balance by 10%. User's balance in the `ERC20Rebasing` contract reflects 1100 USDB due to the automatic rebalancing. However, this increase is not accounted for in the locked balance.



### Attempting to Unlock:

```solidity

// User attempts to unlock 1000 USDB

lockManager.unlock(tokenAddress, 1000 * 10**18);

```



### Potential Errors:

- The `lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenAddress].quantity` in `LockManager` remains 1000 USDB, ignoring the rebased yield.

- The additional 100 USDB yield is not accessible or claimable, effectively resulting in a loss for the user.



## Tools Used

- Manual Review





## Recommended Mitigation Steps



### Regular Updates to Locked Amounts:

Implement a mechanism to update locked amounts regularly by querying the rebased balance from the `ERC20Rebasing` contract. This ensures yields from rebasing are accurately reflected and claimable.

        // Transfer erc tokens

The `proposeUSDPrice()` function in the contract automatically records the proposer's approval and increments the `approval count` upon proposal creation. # Vulnerability details

## Impact
The lockOnBehalf function allows an attacker to repeatedly force a harvest operation on a victim user by passing zero ETH and zero quantity to a lockOnBehalf call where the OnBehalfOf is the victim. This results in a Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack that prevents the victim from accumulating Schnibbles rewards over time.
in fact forceHarvest must be called only from wallets authorized by the user who is involved in the harvest, not just anyone can do it, otherwise this problem arises also because inside (_harvest) there is a division for /1 days which ultimately helps this problem making the rounding down.

## Proof of Concept
1) The attacker calls the lockOnBehalf function with the following parameters:
```
    _tokenContract: address(0)
    _quantity: 0
    _onBehalfOf: Address of the victim user
    msg.value: 0
```
hypothetical transaction (could be tested in the current suit):
```
it("should lock token for other player", async () => {
        const { request } = await testContracts.lockManager.contract.simulate.lockOnBehalf(
          [zeroAddress, parseEther("0"), alice],
          { account: bob, value: parseEther("0") }
        );
        const txHash = await testClient.writeContract(request);
        await assertLockSuccess({
          testContracts,
          testERC20Contract,
          numberNFTs: 0n,
          player: alice,
          quantity: parseEther("0"),
          lockedQuantity: parseEther("0"),
          remainder: 0n,
          sender: bob,
          tokenContractAddress: zeroAddress,
          txHash,
        });
      });
```
2) This call goes through the following steps:
    1) The lockOnBehalf function checks the parameters and calls the _lock function.
    2) In _lock, the accountManager.forceHarvest(_lockRecipient); line forces a harvest for the victim.
    3) The _harvest function calculates the Schnibbles to be harvested based on the elapsed time since the last harvest. Since the attacker makes frequent calls (like one every few hours), the elapsed time is very short, and the rewards are negligible (rounded to zero).
    4) The lastHarvestDate of the victim is updated, preventing the accumulation of Schnibbles rewards over time.

repeat this process every few hours,depending on how much the victim has in the protocol(getDailySchnibbles)

## Tools Used
manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
add an allowance mapping that tracks every delegation,like so:
``
mapping(address account => mapping(address spender => bool)) private _allowances;
``
and add the checks as a modifier like so:
```
    modifier onlyAuthorized(address onBehalfOf){
        if (!_allowances[onBehalfOf][msg.sender])revert NotAuthorized();
        _;
        }
```
that allows only authorized parties to lock tokens on behalf of other users.


## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L374-L377


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `_lock` function in the smart contract does not correctly handle the result of the `transferFrom` call when transferring ERC20 tokens. This oversight allows an attacker to lock tokens without actually transferring them to the contract, which can lead to unauthorized access and withdrawal of tokens from the protocol.
## Proof of Concept
```javascript  
function _lock(
    address _tokenContract,
    uint256 _quantity,
    address _tokenOwner,
    address _lockRecipient
) private {
    // ... (other code)

    
    if (_tokenContract != address(0)) {
        IERC20 token = IERC20(_tokenContract);
@>      token.transferFrom(_tokenOwner, address(this), _quantity);
    }

    // ... (other code)
}
```
The function `token.transferFrom(_tokenOwner, address(this), _quantity)` is called without checking its return value. According to the ERC20 standard, `transferFrom` should return a boolean indicating the success of the transfer. If the transfer fails the function returns false, but the current implementation does not handle this case, and the _lock function proceeds to update the contract state as if the transfer succeeded.

Imagine this scenario:
  1. An attacker can approve the contract to spend tokens from an account that 
     does not hold sufficient tokens.
  2. Call the `lock` function to lock the tokens.
  3. The `transferFrom` call fails, but _lock function continues and incorrectly 
     records the tokens as locked.
  4. The attacker can later call the unlock function to withdraw tokens that were 
     never actually transferred to the contract.

## Tools Used
manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use the OpenZeppelin SafeERC20 library to ensure that all ERC20 token transfers are correctly handled. The SafeERC20 library provides wrappers around the ERC20 operations that handle cases where the token contract does not return a boolean or returns false on failure.


## Assessed type

ERC20

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L177-L242


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

The protocol employs five price feeds to establish a consensus on the USD value of an asset. These feeds vote to approve or disapprove proposed prices. A price is finalized only after reaching a predefined approval or disapproval threshold. However, if neither threshold is met due to insufficient consensus among the feeds, it results in a deadlock, preventing any new price proposals and leading to the use of outdated prices.

## Vulnerability Detail

the `approveUSDPrice` and `disapproveUSDPrice` functions are critical for voting on proposed prices. Once a proposal accumulates enough votes to reach either threshold, it is either executed or rejected, respectively:

- approveUSDPrice
```solidity=202
if (usdUpdateProposal.approvalsCount >= APPROVE_THRESHOLD) {
            _execUSDPriceUpdate();
        }
```

- disapproveUSDPrice
```solidity=237
if (usdUpdateProposal.disapprovalsCount >= DISAPPROVE_THRESHOLD) {
            delete usdUpdateProposal;
```
and then it's deleted. it's the only way to delete a proposal.
Proposals are introduced through the `proposeUSDPrice` function, which cannot proceed if there is an ongoing proposal:

```solidity=142
function proposeUSDPrice(
        uint256 _price,
        address[] calldata _contracts
    )
        external
        onlyOneOfRoles(
            [
                Role.PriceFeed_1,
                Role.PriceFeed_2,
                Role.PriceFeed_3,
                Role.PriceFeed_4,
                Role.PriceFeed_5
            ]
        )
    {
=>        if (usdUpdateProposal.proposer != address(0))
```

The inability to propose new prices until the current proposal is resolved can lead to a deadlock. For instance, if the thresholds are misaligned with voting behaviors (e.g., approveThreshold=3, disapproveThreshold=4) and only 2 approve while 3 disapprove, the proposal remains active and unresolved. This scenario prevents the admin from adjusting the thresholds due to existing constraints:

```solidity=128
function setUSDThresholds(
        uint8 _approve,
        uint8 _disapprove
    ) external onlyAdmin {
        if (usdUpdateProposal.proposer != address(0))
            revert ProposalInProgressError();
```

Additionally, price feeds are unable to revise their votes as the system does not permit revoting or vote cancellation:

- approveUSDPrice
```solidity=177
if (usdUpdateProposal.approvals[msg.sender] == _usdProposalId)
            revert ProposalAlreadyApprovedError();
```

Even attempts by the admin to change the roles of the price feeds are ineffective once they have voted, leading to a scenario where the price reporting system can become inoperable. This vulnerability makes the system susceptible to stagnation, where unresolved proposals prevent the updating of price feeds, significantly impacting the protocol's functionality.

## Impact

This deadlock results in a Denial of Service (DOS) within the price reporting system, causing the protocol to operate with stale prices. Consequently, this affects the accurate calculation of user TVLs and leads to incorrect distribution of rewards.

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

add a period where if the proposed price isn't accepted or rejected , then it should be deleted to allow proposers to propose a new price.

- proposeUSDPrice
```diff=142
function proposeUSDPrice(
        uint256 _price,
        address[] calldata _contracts
    )
        external
        onlyOneOfRoles(
            [
                Role.PriceFeed_1,
                Role.PriceFeed_2,
                Role.PriceFeed_3,
                Role.PriceFeed_4,
                Role.PriceFeed_5
            ]
        )
    {
-        if (usdUpdateProposal.proposer != address(0))
+        if (usdUpdateProposal.proposer != address(0) && usdUpdateProposal.proposedDate + cooldown > block.timestamp)
    revert ProposalInProgressError();
```


## Assessed type

DoS

# Vulnerability details

## Summary

In `unlock`, transfer() is used for native ETH withdrawal. The transfer() and send() functions forward a fixed amount of 2300 gas. Historically, it has often been recommended to use these functions for value transfers to guard against reentrancy attacks. However, the gas cost of EVM instructions may change significantly during hard forks which may break already deployed contract systems that make fixed assumptions about gas costs. For example. EIP 1884 broke several existing smart contracts due to a cost increase of the SLOAD instruction.

## Impact

The use of the deprecated transfer() function for an address will inevitably make the transaction fail when:

    The claimer smart contract does not implement a payable function.
    The claimer smart contract does implement a payable fallback which uses more than 2300 gas unit.
    The claimer smart contract implements a payable fallback function that needs less than 2300 gas units but is called through proxy, raising the call's gas usage above 2300.

Additionally, using higher than 2300 gas might be mandatory for some multisig wallets.

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

Use call() instead of transfer().

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275-L398


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

On the Blast chain, USDB and WETH are implemented as rebasing tokens that adjust holders' balances automatically to reflect yield changes. When these tokens are locked in the protocol, users miss out on potential yields due to the tokens' rebasing nature. More critically, during a negative rebase, the protocol may not possess sufficient funds to fulfill all unlock requests, potentially leading to transaction reverts and locked funds.

## Vulnerability Detail

USDB and WETH adjust user balances directly to account for accrued yield or to reflect negative rebasing adjustments. This automatic balance adjustment poses significant risks when these tokens are locked in the lockManager.

The locking mechanism involves transferring tokens from the user to the contract without accounting for future rebasing events:

- _lock
```solidity=347
if (_tokenContract != address(0)) {
    IERC20 token = IERC20(_tokenContract);
    token.transferFrom(_tokenOwner, address(this), _quantity);
}
```

When users request to unlock their tokens, the amount originally locked is returned without any adjustments for accrued yield or loss due to rebasing:

- unlock
```solidity=422
IERC20 token = IERC20(_tokenContract);
token.transfer(msg.sender, _quantity);
```

This process does not compensate for any increase in token balance due to positive rebasing, effectively causing users to lose out on yield. Moreover, in the event of a negative rebase, the lockManager may find itself with fewer tokens than required to satisfy all unlock requests, leading to failed transactions.

## Impact

This vulnerability can result in two significant issues for users:

1. Loss of Yield: Users do not benefit from positive rebasing effects during the lock period, missing out on potential gains.
2. Inability to Unlock Funds: During a negative rebase, the total token supply in the lockManager may decrease below the amount needed to honor all unlock requests, causing user transactions to revert.

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

account for users their yield.


## Assessed type

ERC20

When a user set his `lockDuration` using `setLockDuration()`, it ensures that `unlockTime` is not `reduced` but the problem is instead of adding `block.timestamp` to `_duration` in unlockTime, `lastLockTime` is added, which `reduces` the unlockTime

         @>  lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime = lastLockTime + uint32(_duration);

2. At 5PM, user decided to change his `lockDuration = 3hrs`, so block.timestamp + duration = 5PM + 3hrs = 8PM, ie check pass because 8PM > 7PM(unlockTime)
3. Now, according to above code unlockTime = lastLockTime + duration = 1PM + 3hrs = 4PM, which reduces the unlockTime from 7PM to 4PM

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L364


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The current implementation of the _lock function can lead to inaccurate calculations of the number of NFTs to be awarded when locking tokens with different decimals. This discrepancy arises because the function does not normalize token amounts to a consistent decimal scale before performing arithmetic operations. As a result, users might receive an incorrect number of NFTs, potentially undermining the fairness and accuracy of the system.

Proof of Concept (PoC):


Assume two tokens: Token A with 18 decimals and Token B with 6 decimals.
Let configuredToken.nftCost be 1,000,000,000,000,000,000 (1 * 10^18) for Token A and 1,000,000 (1 * 10^6) for Token B.
A user locks 2 * 10^18 units of Token A and 2 * 10^6 units of Token B.
Current Calculation in the Function:

For Token A:
```
numberNFTs = (2 * 10^18 - 0) / 1,000,000,000,000,000,000 = 2
```
For Token B:
```
numberNFTs = (2 * 10^6 - 0) / 1,000,000 = 2
```
Here, the calculations are correct because the decimals match the nftCost.
Potential Issue with Mismatched Decimals:

If the configuredToken.nftCost was not adjusted for token decimals, the calculation could go wrong. For example, if configuredToken.nftCost for Token A was mistakenly set as 1,000,000 (matching Token B's decimal), the calculation would be:
```
numberNFTs = (2 * 10^18 - 0) / 1,000,000 = 2 * 10^12
```
This would result in an erroneously high number of NFTs, illustrating the need for proper normalization.

## Tools Used
manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Normalize token amounts to a common decimal scale before performing calculations to ensure consistency and accuracy


## Assessed type

Decimal

the `getLockedWeightedValue` function checks to ensure that the player quantity is > 0 as below

Proof of Concept (PoC):

Suppose a user locks tokens for a specific duration.
Once the lock duration expires, the user does not immediately unlock the tokens.
The system calculates the weighted value of the locked tokens using the getLockedWeightedValue function.
Despite the lock duration expiring, the system still considers the tokens as locked and includes them in the calculation.
As a result, the reported weighted value inaccurately includes these tokens, leading to misleading representations of the user's actual locked token holdings.

Manual Review

Implement a mechanism to accurately track and update the status of locked tokens once the lock duration expires.
Consider automatically adjusting the locked status of tokens when the lock duration ends, ensuring that only actively locked tokens are included in weighted value calculations.

```solidity
function setUSDThresholds(
    uint8 _approve,
    uint8 _disapprove
) external onlyAdmin {

        revert ProposalInProgressError();//@audit-info we can't set thresholds while in the process.

    DISAPPROVE_THRESHOLD = _disapprove;

    emit USDThresholdUpdated(_approve, _disapprove);
}
```
The admin can set any threshold value without validation. If the admin incorrectly sets the THRESHOLD to a value greater than 5, for example, 6, then neither approvalsCount nor disapprovalsCount can reach the THRESHOLD.

Since the current proposal can only be deleted when it is either approved or disapproved, it cannot be reset in this scenario.

Furthermore, due to the usdUpdateProposal.proposer != address(0) check, the admin cannot reconfigure the THRESHOLD.

This situation can lead to a system DoS

## Tools Used
Foundry

check `THRESHOLD` is less than 6 when setting it.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
An attacker can call `lockOnBehalf` to extend the user's lockout time before the user is about to be unlocked. The `lockOnBehalf` function does not limit the minimum number of lockouts, so an attacker can spend 1wei of tokens at a time to continually extend the user's lockout time.

When `_lock` function is called, `lockedToken.unlockTime` will be extended:
```solidity
lockedToken.lastLockTime = uint32(block.timestamp);

            uint32(_lockDuration);
```
In `unlock` function, a check is performed on `lockedToken.unlockTime`:
```solidity
if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp))
            revert TokenStillLockedError();
```
So an attacker can keep calling `lockOnBehalf` to extend the lock time, and the user's locked token will never be able to be unlocked.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider setting a minimum number of locked tokens in `_lock` function.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275


# Vulnerability details


## Impact
The `lockOnBehalf` function allows locking tokens on behalf of another player, but it lacks validation to ensure that msg.sender has permission to act on behalf of the player.

## Proof of Concept

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275
```solidity
File: src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275
    function lockOnBehalf(
        address _tokenContract,
        uint256 _quantity,
        address _onBehalfOf
    )
        external
        payable
        notPaused
        onlyActiveToken(_tokenContract)
        onlyConfiguredToken(_tokenContract)
        nonReentrant
    {
        address tokenOwner = msg.sender;
        address lockRecipient = msg.sender;
        if (_onBehalfOf != address(0)) {
            lockRecipient = _onBehalfOf;
        }

        _lock(_tokenContract, _quantity, tokenOwner, lockRecipient);
    }
```

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Implement proper authorization checks in the `lockOnBehalf` function to ensure that `msg.sender` has explicit permission to act on behalf of the player.
This can be achieved by incorporating an approval mechanism.


## Assessed type

Access Control

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L344-L345
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L352-L355
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L379


# Vulnerability details

Currently the value of `lockedToken.remainder` will be updated if `lock()` gets called during a lockdrop. However, the `lockedToken.remainder` will be reset to zero if `lock()` gets called during a non lockdrop period.

## Proof of Concept

Assume a period of lockdrops and no lockdrops.

```javascript
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
//  lockdrop_1 | no_lockdrop_1 | lockdrop_2 | no_lockdrop_2 | lockdrop_3
```

Also assume

- `_quantity = 7e18` (all calls)
- `configuratedToken.nftCost = 8e18` (all calls)
- `lockedToken.remainder = 0` (first call of each scenario, A.1 and B.1)

Scenario A

1. Bob calls `lock()` during `lockdrop_1`, resulting in `quantity = 7e18`, `remainder = 7e18` and `numberNFTs = 0`.
2. Bob calls `lock()` during `lockdrop_2`, resulting in `quantity = 15e18`, `remainder = 7e18` and `numberNFTs = 1`.
3. Bob calls `lock()` during `lockdrop_3`, resulting in `quantity = 15e18`, `remainder = 7e18` and `numberNFTs = 1`.

Scenario B

1. Same as 1.a above.
2. Bob calls `lock()` during `no_lockdrop_2`, resulting in `quantity = 15e18`, `remainder = 0` (branch for lockdrop not called).
3. Bob calls `lock()` during `lockdrop_3`, resulting in `quantity = 7e18`, `remainder = 7e18` and `numberNFTs = 0`.

Effectively, the issue is that if it's not a lockdrop period, the state variable `lockedToken.remainder` will have the value of the local `remainder` variable, which will still be zero since the branch for lockdrop will not be executed.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L344-L345

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L352-L355

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L379

## Impact

If the poc example, we can see the value of `numberNFTs` will be different during `lockdrop_3` depending if he called `lock()` during `lockdrop_2` or `no_lockdrop_2`.

Therefore, the `nftOverloard.addReveal()` can have a smaller number of NFTs if the user previously called `lock()` during a non lockdrop period, since the remainder is not carried over.

It's also possible for a mallicious user to call `lockOnBehalf` during a non lockdrop period for another user with 1 wei to forcefully reset his remainder.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L369

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

One approach can be to move `lockedToken.remainder = remainder` inside the lockdrop conditional branch so it only gets updated during lockdrop periods.

```diff
diff --git a/LockManager.sol b/LockManager.updated.sol
--- a/LockManager.sol
+++ b/LockManager.updated.sol
@@ -367,6 +367,8 @@ contract LockManager is BaseBlastManager, ILockManager, ReentrancyGuard {

                 // Tell nftOverlord that the player has new unopened Munchables
                 nftOverlord.addReveal(_lockRecipient, uint16(numberNFTs));
+
+                lockedToken.remainder = remainder;
             }
         }

@@ -376,7 +378,6 @@ contract LockManager is BaseBlastManager, ILockManager, ReentrancyGuard {
             token.transferFrom(_tokenOwner, address(this), _quantity);
         }

-        lockedToken.remainder = remainder;
         lockedToken.quantity += _quantity;
         lockedToken.lastLockTime = uint32(block.timestamp);
```



## Assessed type

Timing

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L249-L269
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L347
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L382-L384


# Vulnerability details

If the player manages to call `setLockDuration()` before a token is configurated, he can set 1 second of lockup time and unlock almost immediately everytime he locks during a non lockdrop period. These's also another scenario which he can set 1 second if he doesn't have any locked tokens.

## Proof of Concept

- Player is monitoring events for Munchable contracts and after initial deployment he manages to call `setLockDuration()` with `_duration = 1` before any call is made to `configureToken()`.
- Everytime the player locks any token via `lock()` during a non lockdrop period, he will be able to unlock almost immediately, e.g. after 2 seconds, since `_lockDuration` will evaluate to 1 and `lockToken.unlockTime` will evaluate to `block.timestamp + 1`. The check for `lock.unlockTime` will pass in [unlock](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L410-L411).

This is possible because `setLockDuration()` won't interate the [configurateTokens loop](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L249-L269), and the lockup time only reverts when `_lockDuration` is smaller than configurated minimum [during lockup periods](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L352-L360) in `lock()`.

There's also another scenario which would be for the player to call `setLockDuration()` with `_duration = 1` without having any lock tokens (meaning [revert check won't be executed](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L254-L261)). With this approach, his `lockToken.unlockTime` will also be very small when evaluated in `lock()`.

## Impact

This would allow players to harvest the rewards almost immediately without having to wait for lockup times, and call `unlock()` right after calling `lock()`.

## Tools Used

Manual review.

## Recommented Mitigation Steps

One approach could be to check if `_duration` is not smaller than a default min value in `setLockDuration()`.

Another approach could be to update `_lockDuration` in `lock()` to be the value of `lockdrop.minLockDuration` when `_lockDuration` is smaller then `lockdrop.minLockDuration`, because currently it updates if `_lockDuration` [is zero](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L347-L351).



## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401-L404


# Vulnerability details

## Description
As per the [README.md](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables?tab=readme-ov-file#general-questions), which is the source of truth:
```md
USDB, WETH, (assume we can add more to the future for use in LockManager)
``` 
and:
[ERC20 token behaviors in scope](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables?tab=readme-ov-file#erc20-token-behaviors-in-scope)
```md
Balance changes outside of transfers | YES
```
This means that rebase tokens should be treated as in-scope and they can be added in the future to the LockManager contract.
Usage of rebase tokens can lead to players losing their funds. If a negative rebase happens, the users that have their tokens locked for the longest time will lose their funds.
## Proof of Concept
- 100 users have all deposited `1 stETH` each which can negative rebase as per [Lido.fi docs](https://docs.lido.fi/integrations/aave/specification/).
- The total amount deposited is `100 stETH`.
- A negative rebase happens of `-1%`.
- The total amount deposited is now `99 stETH`.
- 99 users call `LockManager.unlock()`, which takes the `quantity` that was deposited:
```javascript
    function unlock(
        address _tokenContract,
        uint256 _quantity
    ) external notPaused nonReentrant {
        ...
        } else {
            IERC20 token = IERC20(_tokenContract);
            token.transfer(msg.sender, _quantity);
        }
    ...
```
- This means that the 100th user will not be able get his initial `1 stETH` deposit, resulting in a `1 stETH` loss.
## Tools used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
When using rebase tokens, assign a ratio claim to the users of said tokens.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L257-L258
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L265-L267


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The lock duration can be set to a time before the existing unlock time

## Proof of Concept
The lock duration check in `setLockDuration` only checks if the duration is below the current time + _duration, it however sets unlock time to lastLockTime + _duration

This can allow an user to set an unlock time before the existing unlock time.

~ Alice sets unlock time to time 2000.
Last time is now 1000, and _duration is 1000,

Time is now - 1500
Alice calls setLockDuration again with _duration as 501
The check 1500 + 501 > 2000 passes

However the unlock time would be mistakenly set as 1000 + 501 ~ 1501
allowing Alice to break the invariant and prepone the unlock time


## Tools Used
Manual analysis

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
use correct check that is 
`lastLockTime + uint32(_duration) < lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime` 
instead of 
`uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <                 lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime`





## Assessed type

Other

# Vulnerability details

## Description
While having role-based access control mechanisms like in the LockManager contract is generally a good practice. But in this case, any address with one of the specified roles can propose USD price without any other require or access check. This could lead to unauthorized changes in USD price proposals.

## Impact
- Unauthorized addresses with the specified roles can propose, approve, or disapprove USD price updates, leading to potential manipulation of the price data.

## Proof of Concept
- A malicious user gains access to an address with one of the specified roles (`Role.PriceFeed_1`) etc.
- The attacker calls the `proposeUSDPrice`, `approveUSDPrice`, or `disapproveUSDPrice` function to propose, approve, or disapprove a USD price update when it shouldn't have access.
[LockManager: 142-172](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142-L174)

## Tools Used
Manual Code Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add additional access control checks to ensure that only authorized addresses can propose, approve, or disapprove USD price. This can be achieved by implementing a more robust access control mechanism such as requiring specific addresses to be whitelisted or requiring multi-signature approvals.

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L376


# Vulnerability details

In the [LockManager.sol](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol) contract, users can lock his `WETH` to mint new Munchable NFTs and/or migrate existing ones. This is done by calling the [lock()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L297C5-L309C6) function, which calls [_lock()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L311). The [_lock()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L311) function sets `msg.sender` as the `_tokenOwner` and handles the logic for locking tokens.

However, the transfer of ERC tokens is done using [token.transferFrom()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L376). 
This approach works well on most chains (Ethereum, Optimism, Polygon, BSC, ...) that use the [standard WETH9 contract](https://github.com/gnosis/canonical-weth/blob/master/contracts/WETH9.sol#L65C6-L68C10).
This contract handles the case where `src == msg.sender`:

```solidity
WETH9.sol:
        if (src != msg.sender && allowance[src][msg.sender] != uint(- 1)) {
            require(allowance[src][msg.sender] >= wad);
            allowance[src][msg.sender] -= wad;
        }
```

The problem is that the `WETH` implementation on `Blast` uses [a different contract](https://blastscan.io/address/0x4300000000000000000000000000000000000004#code), and does not have this `src == msg.sender` handling.

## Impact

The transfer incompatibility issue in the [LockManager.sol](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol) contract prevents users from locking their `WETH` tokens on `Blast`.

## Proof of Concept

https://gist.github.com/cholakovvv/7cc4b7f62e70569505b7ab29c195b607

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

To address this issue, it's recommended to modify the `LockManager.sol` file as follows:

```diff
src/managers/LockManager.sol:
374:    if (_tokenContract != address(0)) {
375:         IERC20 token = IERC20(_tokenContract);
-376:        token.transferFrom(_tokenOwner, address(this), _quantity);
+376:        token.transfer(address(this), _quantity);
377:    }
```

> If the protocol team plans to implement different tokens on other chains, keep in mind that the same issue exists with [Wrapped Arbitrum](https://arbiscan.io/address/0x8b194beae1d3e0788a1a35173978001acdfba668#code) and  [Wrapped Fantom](https://ftmscan.com/token/0x21be370d5312f44cb42ce377bc9b8a0cef1a4c83#code).
>


## Assessed type

Error

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L414
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L366
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L476-L482
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L202-L204


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`LockManager` allows users to lock tokens in return for `rewards`. They can unlock their tokens once their respective `unlockTime` has passed.

When users unlock their tokens, `AccountManager::forceHarvest()` is called, which gives users rewards based off the `USD` value of their locked tokens.

This `USD` value can be changed at anytime by a `proposer` with `Pricefeed` role via a call to `proposeUSDPrice()`.

If a minimum number of `Pricefeed` roles approve the new `USD` value, that value with then be updated.

This leads to a step-wise jump vulnerability, where if the `USD` value suddenly changes then users will get rewards based off that `USD` value for the entire time they locked their tokens.

For example, if a user locks `5000 USD` of tokens for `10 days`, but then the value changes to `1000 USD` for the next `5 days` via `proposeUSDPrice()`, the user will get `1000 USD` of rewards for the entire `15 days`, when they should get `5000 USD` for the first `10 days` and `1000` for `5 days`. The user will suffer in this case.

## Proof of Concept
When users unlock their tokens, the following call is made

[LockManager.sol#L414](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L414)
```javascript
    // force harvest to make sure that they get the schnibbles that they are entitled to
    accountManager.forceHarvest(msg.sender);
```

These are rewards earned based off the user's `locked weighted value`

[AccountManager.sol#L366](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/AccountManager.sol#L366)
```javascript
uint256 weightedValue = lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_caller);
```

The `locked weighted value` is based off the user's locked `quantity` and the respective `usdPrice` for the token.

[LockManager.sol#L476-L482](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L476-L482)
```javascript
lockedWeighted += (deltaDecimal * lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]].quantity * configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]] .usdPrice) / 1e18;
```

The `usdPrice` for tokens can change via [proposeUSDPrice()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L142).

If enough approvals are received for the new proposed `usdPrice`, it is officially updated.

[LockManager.sol#L202-L204](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L202-L204)
```javascript
if (usdUpdateProposal.approvalsCount >= APPROVE_THRESHOLD) {
            _execUSDPriceUpdate();
    }
```

As explained in the example from above, if the USD value suddenly drops, the user will receive rewards based off that USD amount for the entire time they locked their tokens.

Conversely, if the token value goes up, they will receive rewards based off the new USD value for the entire time locked.

The correct solution is to give users the respective reward based off what the USD value was at that time (i.e, if USD value is 5000 for first 10 days and 1000 for next 5 days, give users reward for 5000 USD for first 10 days and 1000 for 5 days, rather than 1000 USD for the full 15 days).

## Tools Used
Manual Review.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Prior to updating the `USD price` of the tokens, update all user rewards, so they can still receive rewards based off what the `USD price` was at that point in time.





## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L14


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Yield for `USDB` and `WETH` tokens are lost

## Proof of Concept
The protocol mentioned in the contest README that [Balance changes outside transfers](https://code4rena.com/audits/2024-05-munchables#top:~:text=ERC20%20token%20behaviors%20in%20scope) are in-scope.

The protocol will be deployed on `Blast Mainnet`, where `USDB` and `WETH` automatically accrue yield. 

There is no function that can retrieve the accrued yield from these tokens, and since users who lock tokens will only be able to unlock the same amount of tokens they originally locked, the yield accrued will be lost.

## Tools Used
Manual review.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Implement a function to retrieve the yield generated from these tokens

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Impact: High, as value can be stuck forever
Likelihood: Low
Overall medium

## Proof of Concept

LockManager.sol contract has `receive` and `fallback` functions that are `payable`. If someone sends a transaction with `msg.value != 0` then the ETH will be `stuck` in the contract forever without a way for anyone to withdraw it.

```
fallback() external payable {
        revert LockManagerInvalidCallError();
    }

    receive() external payable {
        revert LockManagerRefuseETHError();
    }
```

A contract is able to receive funds with the payable attribute must have a withdraw function to secure that funds can be sent out from the contract or remove payable attribute.


## Tools Used

manual

Best practice here is to implement a function that is used for withdrawing the stuck ETH, or just remove the fallback and receive functions.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L420


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The use of `transfer()` for transferring ETH in the `unlock()` function can result in transaction failures due to the fixed gas stipend of 2300 gas units forwarded by `transfer()`. This can be problematic in the following cases:
1. If the recipient contract has a fallback function that requires more than 2300 gas, the transfer will fail.
2. Changes in gas costs, such as those introduced by [EIP-1884](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1884), can increase the gas required for operations within the fallback function, making previously functioning contracts fail. [Gas Cost Increase for SLOAD, BALANCE and EXTCODEHASH](https://chainsecurity.com/istanbul-hardfork-eips-increasing-gas-costs-and-more/#:~:text=Therefore%2C%20EIP%2D1884%20raises%20the,from%20400%20to%20700%20gas.)
3. If the recipient contract is called through a proxy, the additional gas usage can exceed 2300 gas.
4. Some multisig wallets require more than 2300 gas for their operations.

As a result, users may find themselves unable to unlock their ETH from the contract, leading to locked funds.

## Proof of Concept
[LockManager.sol#L420](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L420) `payable(msg.sender).transfer(_quantity)`

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use `call()` instead of `transfer()`.

You can read more here:
https://swcregistry.io/docs/SWC-134/
https://consensys.io/diligence/blog/2019/09/stop-using-soliditys-transfer-now/


## Assessed type

ETH-Transfer

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L374-L377


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In the [LockManager::_lock](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L311-L371) function, the `transferFrom()` is used to actually transfer the tokens from the owner to the contract. According to the ERC20 standard, the transfer function "returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded" ([OZ's Docs](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/2.x/api/token/erc20#IERC20-transferFrom-address-address-uint256-)). If the transfer fails and returns false, the function will proceed as if the transfer was successful. The impact is that for an arbitrary ERC20 token, this `transferFrom()` call may return `false` but the `_lock()` logic will miss that, and assume it was successfully transferred into the contract and updates the `lockedToken.quantity += _quantity` accounting accordingly. This will result in the user locking tokens for free.

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L374-L377

1. Alice wants to lock 10000 ERC20 tokens and calls the `lock()` function.
2. The `transferFrom` inside `_lock` fails due to exceeding the gas limit and returns `false`.
3. However, the return value is not checked, and the execution succeeds, adding the quantity into the lockedToken `lockedToken.quantity += _quantity`.
4. Alice successfully locked 10000 token for free.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Check the success boolean of the `transferFrom()` call. Alternatively, use OZ’s `SafeERC20’s safeTransferFrom()` function.


## Assessed type

Token-Transfer

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Allowing users to receive more schnibbles than entitled.

## Proof of Concept
In the `unlock` function, there is no check for a zero quantity, allowing users to call `accountManager.forceHarvest(msg.sender);` with a quantity of 0. This results in schnibbles being harvested even when no tokens are actually unlocked.

Code : https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401

The issue can be exploited as follows:

- Alice locks 10 WETH tokens.
- Alice calls the unlock function with the tokenContract and a quantity of 0.
- This bypasses the following checks:
`
if (lockedToken.quantity < _quantity) revert InsufficientLockAmountError();
if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp)) revert TokenStillLockedError();
`
- `accountManager.forceHarvest(msg.sender);` is called.
- Since the quantity is 0, no tokens leave the contract, and Alice can call this function again, potentially leading to an unintended increase in schnibbles.
(as the `_harvest` calls `getDailySchnibbles` which takes the value from `getLockedWeightedValue` which returns same everytime.)

The same can be done with the `_lock` function. After locking some tokens, one can call it with a quantity of 0. However, in this case, only schnibbles can be harvested as no NFTs are obtained.

## Tools Used
manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

add something like this at the start of the `_lock` and `unlock` functions.
`if (_quantity == 0) revert InvalidLockQuantityError();`





## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Loss of tokens for the Owner who called the `lockOnBehalf` function.

## Proof of Concept
In the `lockOnBehalf` function, if a user locks tokens on behalf of another user and mistakenly uses the wrong user address, the tokens will be locked in the contract under the wrong user's account. As a result, the wrong user can unlock these tokens, leading to potential loss of tokens for the intended user.

Scenario:
- User A intends to lock tokens on behalf of User B but mistakenly uses User C's address.
- User A calls lockOnBehalf with User C's address as the _onBehalfOf parameter, locking tokens for User C instead of User B.
- User C, the unintended recipient, can now unlock the tokens that were mistakenly locked for him, leading to a loss of tokens for User B.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add 2 step verification for the call in which OnBehalf confirms the transaction.
(Or)
In the ERC20 standard, if User A mistakenly approves tokens for User C instead of User B, User A can later correct this by calling approve with 0 tokens for User C. This revokes the approval, ensuring that User C cannot spend the tokens. However, in the current contract's lockOnBehalf function, there is no similar mechanism to revoke the lock in case of a mistake.




## Assessed type

DoS

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L506-L528


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.
### Issue: Incomplete Deletion of Mapping in USD Price Update Function

**Location:**
- `LockManager._execUSDPriceUpdate()` (src/managers/LockManager.sol: lines 506-527)

**Details:**
- The function deletes `ILockManager.USDUpdateProposal` (src/interfaces/ILockManager.sol: lines 60-69), which includes a mapping.
- Specifically, the line `delete usdUpdateProposal` (src/managers/LockManager.sol: line 525) is intended to remove the proposal.

**Problem:**
- Deleting a structure that contains a mapping does not remove the mapping itself, as per [Solidity Documentation](http://solidity.readthedocs.io/en/develop/types.html#delete).
- Residual data in the mapping may pose a security risk and could potentially be exploited to compromise the contract.

**Recommendation:**
- Implement explicit deletion of all elements within the mapping before deleting the structure to ensure complete removal and mitigate any security risks.

So, instead ```delete usdUpdateProposal;``` you would instead write ```delete usdUpdateProposal[i];``` and loop through each value in the array.

## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

**Bad**
```sol
delete usdUpdateProposal;
```

**Good**
```sol
delete usdUpdateProposal[i];
```
## Tools Used
Slither.
## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Implement a lock mechanism to disable structures containing mappings, rather than deleting them.

So, instead ```delete usdUpdateProposal;``` you would instead write ```delete usdUpdateProposal[i];``` and loop through each value in the array.

**Incorrect**
```sol
delete usdUpdateProposal;
```

**Correct**
```sol
delete usdUpdateProposal[i];
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L473


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The `getLockedWeightedValue` function will always return 0 due to incorrect calculations of `deltaDecimal`. This will cause the functionality for calculating the weighted value to fail.

## Proof of Concept

For example if we have token with 18 decimals `deltaDecimal` will be equal to 10 ** 0 which is 1.

```javascript
uint256 deltaDecimal = 10 **
                    (18 -
                        configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals);
```

Consider an example where the quantity is 100 and the USD price is 100.

```javascript
lockedWeighted +=
                    (deltaDecimal *
                        lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]]
                            .quantity *
                        configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]]
                            .usdPrice) /
                    1e18;
```

For our example, `lockedWeighted` will be `1 * 100 * 100 / 1e18` which is equal to `0.00000000000001`. This value means our `lockedWeighted` will be equal to 0. Even with a bigger price and quantity, our `lockedWeighted` will be 0. The calculations are wrong because the current implementation works with non-decimal numbers but at the end divides by `1e18`.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

```diff
uint256 deltaDecimal = 10 **
-                    (18 - configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals);
+                    (configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals);
```

```diff
lockedWeighted +=
                    (deltaDecimal *
                        lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]]
                            .quantity *
                        configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]]
                            .usdPrice) /
-                    1e18;
+                    (configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals);
```


## Assessed type

Decimal

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L177


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The `approveUSDPrice` function does not check if a user has already disapproved a proposal before approving it. This oversight allows users with the appropriate role to disapprove and then approve the same proposal, which is a security concern.

## Proof of Concept

The `approveUSDPrice` function currently only checks if a user has approved the proposal but does not verify if they have disapproved it. As a result, users who have the role can disapprove a proposal and then approve it afterward. This loophole undermines the integrity of the approval process within the contract.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

According to the documentation, users aim to acquire as many Munchables (NFTs) as possible to earn MUNCH points. An attacker exploiting this vulnerability can obtain more NFTs with less money by locking and unlocking their assets within a very short period.

## Proof of Concept

**Attack Scenario:**
1. The attacker sets their `lockDuration` to 1 second.
2. The attacker locks their assets just enough to receive an NFT (e.g., if the NFT costs 1000 USD, they lock 1000 USD).
3. The attacker then unlocks their assets immediately.
4. The attacker repeats steps 2 and 3 as many times as possible.

By the end of the day, the attacker can accumulate NFTs worth significantly more than 1000 USD in a much shorter time compared to other users.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

This vulnerability exists because the `_lock` function only checks if `lockDuration` is equal to 0. It should instead verify if the `lockDuration` is less than `minLockDuration`.

Suggested code modification:

```diff
-if (_lockDuration == 0) {
+if (_lockDuration < lockdrop.minLockDuration) {
    _lockDuration = lockdrop.minLockDuration;
}
```

By making this change, attackers will be forced to set their `lockDuration` to at least the `lockdrop.minLockDuration`, ensuring the protocol's security.

Context

https://github.com/blast-io/blast/blob/master/blast-geth/params/protocol_params.go#L53)). 

Interacting with a smart contract is a little more expensive than an EOA, so if the locked token owner is a smart contract, there is always a chance in the future that if gas cost change on `Blast` which could make this operation to revert, preventing the player to unlock their ETH token which would be `stuck forever` (for all the players who locked ETH) in the contract, which seems to warrant `High` severity.

This is usuallly a Medium severity issue, but the fact that token would be stuck forever in the contract, which is a `user funds loss`, seems to justify the High severity.

Player unable to unlock their ETH token if gas cost for `opCall` changes unfavorably

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401-L427


# Vulnerability details

In `LockManager.sol` a user can call `lock()` to lock his tokens. If he does so during a lockdrop event he can get NFT reveals deppending on the cost of a single NFT and the quantity of tokens the user deposits. 

If there is a remainder after calculating how many NFTs he should get it gets stored in `lockedToken.remainder` which is added to future locks.
```solidity
uint256 quantity = _quantity + lockedToken.remainder;
...
remainder = quantity % configuredToken.nftCost;
numberNFTs = (quantity - remainder) / configuredToken.nftCost;
...
lockedToken.remainder = remainder;
```

The problem is that there is no way for the user to withdraw this remainder even if he calls the `unlock()` function. In order to get it back he has to lock an additional specific amount of tokens so that there is no remainder left. However he may not have enough funds to do that.

## Impact
Loss of funds for the user

## Proof of Concept
Here is the unlock function:
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401-L427

As you can see it can only return `lockedToken.quantity` back to the user but not `lockedToken.remainder`

Imagine the following scenario:
1. Alice decides to lock 1005e18 tokens
2. The NFT associated with this token costs 1000e18 tokens
3. Alice gets 1 NFT reveal and a remainder of 5e18 tokens which gets stored in `lockedToken.remainder`
4. Alice wants to unlock and withdraw all of her funds but she can't get her remainder back.
5. In order to get it back she has to lock additional 995e18 tokens so that there is no remainder left. She may not have the funds needed to do that.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Allow the user to get `lockedToken.remainder` back using the `unlock()` function



## Assessed type

Other

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If the current time is not within lockdrop start and end period, users can lock tokens with 1 second to bypass the `lockdrop.minLockDuration` restriction. Potentially benefit from the calculated USD value of locked tokens.

## Proof of Concept
The `_lock()` function allows users to lock tokens for a specified duration within a lockdrop period. However, the function does not revert transactions if the current time is outside the lockdrop start and end period.

The `_lock()` function will not revert the transaction if the `block.timestamp` before the `lockdrop.start` or after the `lockdrop.end`, because the check for `_lockDuration` is applied only in the `if` condition. [_lock()#L352](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L352-L360):

```solidity
        if (
            lockdrop.start <= uint32(block.timestamp) &&
            lockdrop.end >= uint32(block.timestamp)
        ) {
            if (
                _lockDuration < lockdrop.minLockDuration ||
                _lockDuration >
                uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))
            ) revert InvalidLockDurationError();
```

Additionally, users can lock tokens with a minimal duration of 1 second, bypassing the `lockdrop.minLockDuration` restriction. [_lock()#L349](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L349-L351):

```solidity
        if (_lockDuration == 0) {
            _lockDuration = lockdrop.minLockDuration;
        }
```

As the `getLockedWeightedValue()` function does not return zero if current time is not within the lock drop period, it returns locked USD value if token prices have been updated to non-zero, allowing users to lock tokens for 1 second and get the calculated USD value of locked tokens.

## Tools Used
vscode

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Revert the transaction if current time is not within the lock drop period.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L461-L487


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Tokens with non-standard decimals could lead to incorrect adjustments, resulting in inaccurate USD value calculations.

## Proof of Concept
The `getLockedWeightedValue()` function calculates the USD value of locked tokens for a player. It assumes tokens have a maximum of 18 decimals and uses this assumption to adjust token quantities.
 
However, readme suggests that ERC20 token behaviours with low decimals(<6) & high decimals(>18) are in scope:
>Low decimals ( < 6)	  Yes
 High decimals ( > 18)	  Yes

Therefore, if a token has more than 18 decimals or fewer than 6 decimals, the ` getLockedWeightedValue()` function may produce incorrect results.

The calculation produces a zero value for any token with more than 18 decimals, severely underestimating the locked value.
```js
    function getLockedWeightedValue(
        address _player
    ) external view returns (uint256 _lockedWeightedValue) {
        uint256 lockedWeighted = 0;
        uint256 configuredTokensLength = configuredTokenContracts.length;
        for (uint256 i; i < configuredTokensLength; i++) {
            if (
                lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]].quantity >
                0 &&
                configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].active
            ) {
                // We are assuming all tokens have a maximum of 18 decimals and that USD Price is denoted in 1e18
                uint256 deltaDecimal = 10 **
                    (18 -
                        configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals);
                lockedWeighted +=
                    (deltaDecimal *
                        lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]]
                            .quantity *
                        configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]]
                            .usdPrice) /
                    1e18;
            }
        }


        _lockedWeightedValue = lockedWeighted;
    }
```
_Simple Example: >18 Decimals_
Quantity: 1,000 tokens
Decimals: 20
USD Price: $1 (1e18)
```js
uint256 deltaDecimal = 10 ** (18 - 20); // Results in 10 ** -2 which is incorrect
lockedWeighted += (deltaDecimal * 1000 * 1e18) / 1e18; // This results in incorrect value
```
_Simple Example: <6 Decimals_
Quantity: 1,000 tokens
Decimals: 4
USD Price: $1 (1e18)
```js
uint256 deltaDecimal = 10 ** (18 - 4); // Results in 10 ** 14
```
```js
lockedWeighted += (1e14 * 1000 * 1e18) / 1e18; // lockedWeighted += 1e14 * 1000
```
This results in:
```js
lockedWeighted += 1e17; // A very large value
```
The calculation produces an excessively large value, potentially causing incorrect weighted value representation.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Adjust the `getLockedWeightedValue()` function for tokens with non-standard decimals


## Assessed type

Decimal

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L356-L360
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L246-L247


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
There are multiple issues that can arise when it comes to changing the maximum lock duration, as well as some instances with the minimum lock duration.

- If the maximum lock duration is ever decreased, users which have had the previous maximum duration will be able to bypass it when staking outside of lockdrop events.
- The minimum lock duration can also be bypassed outside of lockdrop events. 
- Due to a missing minimum lock duration check when calling `setLockDuration`, if it's set below a certain minimum during a lock drop event (or prior to it), the `_lock` function will keep reverting.  

## Proof of Concept
When a user locks their funds (or someone else does on their behalf), the checks for whether the lock time is less than the minimum one or above the maximum one is present in the code block which is only executed during lockdrop events.

```
 if (lockdrop.start <= uint32(block.timestamp) && lockdrop.end >= uint32(block.timestamp)) {
            if (
                _lockDuration < lockdrop.minLockDuration
                    || _lockDuration > uint32(configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxLockDuration))
            ) revert InvalidLockDurationError();
```

If the lockdrop event has passed / isn't set, but the maximum lock duration was decreased in the meantime, users which have had their "old maximum lock period" decide to lock their funds outside of lockdrop events will be able to bypass this and still lock them for the "old maximum".

- Current max lock duration(`StorageKey.MaxLockDuration`) is 90 days.
- Bob has his `lockDuration` set at 90 days.
- Protocol admin decreases the maximum lock duration to 80 days.
- Bob will still be able to lock his tokens for a duration of 90 days (even now the maximum is 80) outside of lockdrop events. 

The above also goes for minimum lock times (even though they're particularly connected to lockdrop events).

The other problem is that there is no check for minimum duration times when calling `setLockDuration` allowing users to set the lock duration below the minimum which would cause the `_lock` function to revert during lockdrop events.

The above scenario can be especially problematic if the minimum duration that a user has set is below the minimum amount and the user expects someone else to lock the funds on their behalf, this will lead to constant reverts, until the lock period is changed and set above the minimum one.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L408-L409
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L380


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Since USDB and WETH are the tokens in-scope, and since balance changes outside of transfers is a token behavior which is in-scope for this audit as well, the lock manager is incompatible with both tokens as it's not designed to support yield-bearing tokens, and both USDB and WETH yield mode are AUTOMATIC by default.

## Proof of Concept

Similar to ETH, WETH and USDB on Blast is also rebasing and follows the same yield mode configurations.

However, unlike ETH where contracts have Disabled yield by default, WETH and USDB accounts have Automatic yield by default for both EOAs and smart contracts.

As per the Blast documentation: https://docs.blast.io/building/guides/weth-yield

When locking funds/tokens in the Lock Manager, the `amount` that we lock is saved as `quantity`:

```
        lockedToken.quantity += _quantity;
``` 

Later when unlocking tokens, the maximum amount of tokens that a user can unlock is the amount that they've locked, i.e. its based on internal accounting values.

```
        if (lockedToken.quantity < _quantity)
            revert InsufficientLockAmountError();
```

This means that any distributed yield won't be able to be claimed by users nor the protocol, i.e. is lost.



## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Implement a way to claim the yield / user balances to change accordingly to the rebases.

The yield mode can also be set as `CLAIMABLE` so that the balances can remain the same (i.e. internal accounting values can be used), but the yield can still be claimed separately: 

https://docs.blast.io/building/guides/weth-yield





## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users lock can be extended by a malicious user with just 1 or 0 wei deposit and this would also cause [`setLockDuration()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L245) to always revert because the unlock time will be constantly increasing. As a result user funds will not be retrievable until the attacker stops making deposits on the behalf of the user.

## Proof of Concept
A user can lock tokens by using [`lock()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L297) or somebody else can lock tokens on behalf of the user with [`lockOnBehalf()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L275).

When a lock is made the unlockTime gets updated with the user configured lock duration:

Reference: [`link`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L379-L384)
```solidity
    ...
    lockedToken.remainder = remainder;
    lockedToken.quantity += _quantity;
    lockedToken.lastLockTime = uint32(block.timestamp);
@>  lockedToken.unlockTime =
        uint32(block.timestamp) +
        uint32(_lockDuration);
    ...
```

Both [`unlock()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L401) and [`setLockDuration()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L245) will be affected and will revert each time the attacker extends the lock:

Reference: [`link`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L410-L411)
```solidity
    if (lockedToken.unlockTime > uint32(block.timestamp))
        revert TokenStillLockedError();
```

Reference: [`link`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-munchables/blob/57dff486c3cd905f21b330c2157fe23da2a4807d/src/managers/LockManager.sol#L256-L261)
```solidity
    if (
        uint32(block.timestamp) + uint32(_duration) <
        lockedTokens[msg.sender][tokenContract].unlockTime
    ) {
        revert LockDurationReducedError();
    }
```

So with just 1 or 0 wei an attacker can extend the lock of a user and can continue to do this as much as he wants. The only expense he has are the gas fee costs.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Introduce mechanisms that will make it harder for a malicious user to extend the lock duration of a user or remove this opportunity entirely.

Such mechanisms could include adding a minimum lock token amount check or allow the user to create a whitelist of addresses that can make locks on his behalf.
